item.title: Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack
item.description:
Boston Scientific Exposes 117,000 Records Following Voice Phishing Attack

Boston Scientific, a Massachusetts-based medical device manufacturer, is sending data breach notices to individuals after a cyberattack exposed personal and medical information belonging to 117,789 people in the United States. The incident marks the second cybersecurity event for the company this year.

🔍 Overview

The attack exposed cloud-based applications and cloud-hosted data between May 7 and May 1, 2025. Boston Scientific became aware of the unauthorized access on May 12. A subsequent investigation determined that a data breach occurred on November 5. The exposed information included personal details and medical information for individuals in multiple U.S. states.

🧩 How it works

According to notification samples shared with U.S. authorities, the hacker gained access to the company’s cloud infrastructure using social engineering in a voice phishing (vishing) attack.

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Exposed: Personal details and medical information.
  • Data Not Exposed: The notification specifies that patient medical records, data from remote monitoring systems, connected medical devices, and clinical case management or workflow applications were not exposed.
  • Scope: The incident impacted 117,789 individuals according to the Texas Attorney General breach portal.
  • Business Impact: The company stated there was no disruption to manufacturing, ordering, distribution, or service to patients and healthcare providers, and no impact on operations, performance, remote monitoring, or the safety of its products.

📊 Incident Comparison

This breach is distinct from a previous cyberattack disclosed on August 25, which caused network outages and global operational disruptions. A Boston Scientific spokesperson confirmed the most recent incident is unrelated to the August 2026 intrusion; a CrowdStrike investigation into that earlier attack found no evidence that attackers compromised cloud applications.

💡 Why it matters

As one of the world’s largest medical device manufacturers with more than 59,000 employees, 13 manufacturing facilities, and a presence in 127 countries, Boston Scientific’s data security is critical. The company contained the incident, investigated with outside cybersecurity experts, and notified law enforcement. However, the company is not offering free credit monitoring and instead recommends impacted individuals use free credit reports, place fraud alerts, and consider credit freezes.

#databreach #cybersecurity #medicaldevices #vishing #BostonScientific

Source: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info

item.title: pCloud Pass users report unauthorized device connections following cyberattack
item.description:
pCloud Pass users report unauthorized device connections following cyberattack

The pCloud Pass password manager was recently targeted by a cyberattack, resulting in users reporting that unknown devices had connected to their accounts, some with two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled. The attack was contained by the pCloud team, though a small number of user email addresses were exposed.

🔍 Overview

According to pCloud, a cyberattack targeting pCloud Pass occurred and was promptly contained. The company stated that a small number of pCloud Pass user email addresses were exposed and that login attempts were made. The system automatically sent notifications to each of these affected addresses.

⚙️ Key details

  • Users reported receiving notifications warning that an unfamiliar device named “pd” connected to their account from IP address 45.131.244.7 in Luxembourg.
  • The IP address is reportedly part of pCloud’s own infrastructure.
  • Notifications were received by customers who had 2FA enabled.
  • Some users who never used the password manager, including those with deleted storage accounts, also received the alerts.
  • PCloud stated the attack was isolated to the password manager, and cloud storage services were not affected.
  • Passwords, notes, and other information stored in pCloud Pass are encrypted on customer devices and were not compromised.
  • It is unknown whether encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen during the attack.
  • A reader noted that the “Open settings” link in the email notifications pointed to passqa1.pcloud.com, a QA environment, rather than the production site.

💡 Why it matters

Threat actors who obtain encrypted password vaults can attempt to crack them offline, bypassing the service’s login rate limits and two-factor authentication protections. This risk was demonstrated in the 2022 LastPass breach, where stolen encrypted password vaults were linked to cryptocurrency thefts after attackers cracked weak or reused master passwords.

🛡️ Security advice

  • pCloud is warning customers to watch for phishing attacks.
  • The company states it will never ask for master passwords or recovery words over email, phone, or chat.
  • PCloud noted that advancements in artificial intelligence are accelerating the discovery of software vulnerabilities, though it did not state that this specific attack was AI-powered.

#pCloud #PasswordManager #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #2FA

Source: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts

item.title: Zero-Day SQL Injection Enables Command Execution in Cacti Monitoring Platform
item.description:
Zero-Day SQL Injection Enables Command Execution in Cacti Monitoring Platform

A zero‑day SQL injection vulnerability in the open‑source network monitoring tool Cacti was publicly disclosed, accompanied by a proof‑of‑concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable servers.

🔍 Overview

  • The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to inject SQL into the Cacti database.
  • It can modify the commands executed by Cacti’s real‑time poller.
  • The exploit requires the Cacti guest account to be enabled.

🧩 How it Works

  • Attackers store malicious SQL statements in a guest user’s graph display preferences.
  • These preferences are processed by Cacti, executing the SQL.
  • The SQL modifies the poller configuration to run arbitrary OS commands.
  • “I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server user in four requests. No login. No valid API key. No phishing. Just four HTTP requests against the default guest surface,” explains the researcher.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Exploit name: 4HTTP2SHELL (previously 4HTTP2ROOT).
  • Published on Thanksgiving Day by researcher ek0ms savi0r from the Church of Malware.
  • GitHub repository: Sad Girls 0day Club.
  • Tested against Cacti Core 1.2.31; earlier versions may also be vulnerable.
  • The researcher expressed frustration: “Security researchers are not the bad guys. We’re the ones trying to help. We’re the ones who read the docs, wrote the repro, and sent the packet capture,” and “We get cracked because we get gaslit for years by billion dollar companies that treat disclosure like a PR problem.”

🚀 Availability

  • Public PoC released with a video demonstration.
  • The vulnerability was not reported to Cacti before its public release.

💡 Why it Matters

  • Cacti can store credentials and SNMP passphrases used to access network devices; a compromise could expose other systems.
  • Privileges gained depend on the account running the Cacti web server and poller processes; often a low‑privileged web server account rather than root.

📌 Mitigation

  • Deactivate the Cacti guest account.
  • Restrict access to the application’s web interface to trusted networks.
  • Review poller configurations for unexpected commands.
  • Examine application logs for warnings involving non‑numeric values in graph display settings, which could indicate attempted exploitation.

As of November 27, there have been no reports of the vulnerability being exploited in attacks.

#ZeroDay #Cacti #SQLInjection #Cybersecurity #NetworkMonitoring

Source: Unpatched Cacti zero-day with public PoC gives remote code execution

item.title: Major US Infrastructure Outages Are Coincidence, Not Cyberattack
item.description:
Major US Infrastructure Outages Are Coincidence, Not Cyberattack

A recent series of outages affecting major US infrastructure providers, including Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, an unnamed NSA network, and Apple, has raised suspicions of a coordinated cyberattack or conspiracy. Evidence indicates these incidents are unrelated and not the result of any cyberattack, nor are they caused by AI. The failures are attributed to a series of unfortunate coincidences involving old, incrementally patched systems often maintained by hobbyists without adequate backup systems.

🔍 Overview

It has been a difficult week for computerized infrastructure, with outages spanning critical sectors such as aviation, banking, and government. While the simultaneity of these events might suggest a common cause or conspiracy, the evidence clarifies that the incidents are distinct and unrelated. Notably, the failures are not the result of any cyberattack, coordinated or otherwise, and even more surprisingly, they do not seem to be the result of AI.

⚙️ Key Details

The underlying causes of these failures stem from the nature of the technology itself:

  • Age and Maintenance: Much of the infrastructure is old and has been incrementally patched and upgraded over decades.
  • Volunteer Maintenance: A surprising amount of the system is maintained by hobbyists without any recompense.
  • Lack of Redundancy: There often aren’t good backup systems.
  • Centralization: More of the infrastructure is centralized, meaning individual failures have cascading consequences across many different aspects of life and society.
  • Brittleness: Much of the tech infrastructure just barely works; when it fails, it can fail badly.

💡 Why It Matters

Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, and recoverability are essential parts of reliable technology, but they are costs that do not generate near-term profits. Modern shareholder capitalism, particularly private equity, prioritizes near-term profits, squeezing out apparent inefficiencies and positive intangibles. Market competition, which usually nudges companies to provide better services, is often removed in pursuit of these profits. From a quarterly budget perspective, spending on reliability measures is viewed as an inefficiency or waste. Consequently, costs of failure are often pushed onto society, leading to stranded travelers and inaccessible bank accounts. These economic pressures create brittle systems with single points of failure, making them more susceptible to cyberattacks and random mistakes. Fixing these issues requires regulation with enforcement and meaningful fines, as well as stringent antitrust enforcement.

📊 Affected Entities

Entity Status
Microsoft Experienced outage
FAA Experienced outage
A handful of banks Experienced outage
United Airlines Experienced outage
Unnamed classified NSA network Experienced outage; details likely never public
Apple Experienced outage

#Infrastructure #Cybersecurity #Technology #Business

Source: Recent Outages Have Economic Causes - Schneier on Security

item.title: SAP Confirms Cyberattack Involving Source Code Modification
item.description:
SAP Confirms Cyberattack Involving Source Code Modification

SAP has confirmed taking urgent action to protect its customers after detecting suspicious activity in its IT environment, a cyberattack the company tracks under the code name “Project Granite.”

🏢 Company Profile

SAP is one of the world’s largest enterprise software vendors, based in Walddorf, Germany. Key operational details include:

  • Employees: 110,000 across 157 countries
  • Subscribers: 300 million
  • Annual Revenue: Over $40 billion

🔍 Incident Details

According to reports from Der Spiegel, which accessed an internal SAP memo, the attackers breached SAP’s GitHub environment, potentially with the aid of AI tools. Insider sources indicated that authentications tokens were stolen from SAP employees and used to copy and modify source code on GitHub.

Aspect Detail
Internal Code Name Project Granite
Breach Vector GitHub environment
Suspected Aid AI tools
Actions Taken by Attacker Stole authentication tokens; copied and modified source code

🛡️ Offical Response

SAP stated that it prompted all employees to keep project details confidential and implemented necessary measures to preserve service security. A company representative told BleepingComputer:

“SAP has identified suspicious activity and promptly implemented the necessary measures to protect its customers and preserve the security of its services.”

Regarding the scope of the compromise, SAP noted:

“Based on our investigation to date, we have found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data.”

“Our customers trust us to protect their data, and that remains our highest priority. In a highly dynamic threat environment, we will continue to strengthen our security to provide the secure and resilient environment our customers depend on.”

Despite this, SAP has not specified which environments were observed having suspicious activity, nor has it advised customers downloading code or performing updates from specific repositories to take action. A spokesperson declined to share further information on this matter.

☣️ Context

The incident follows a public warning from Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) regarding agentic AI tools that empower cyberattacks, such as ARTEX, CAIRN, and PentAGI. This follows reports from Swiss and Italian national cybersecurity agencies regarding the first detections of large-scale AI-driven cyberattacks targeting critical infrastructure.

#SAP #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #AIsecurity

Source: SAP confirms security incident after suspicious GitHub activity

item.title: US Air Force Cloud One platform breached amid wave of federal cyberattacks
item.description:
US Air Force Cloud One platform breached amid wave of federal cyberattacks

Hackers have reportedly breached the US Air Force’s Cloud One computing platform, adding to a recent wave of cyberattacks affecting US government agencies, including the FBI, CIA, and Treasury Department.

🔍 Overview

The intrusion was discovered within the past month during an upgrade of the cloud platform, disrupting application migrations and software updates. According to one source who spoke to Reuters, the hackers exploited an unidentified software vulnerability to gain access to the platform, potentially exposing sensitive military operational and logistics information. US Cyber Command has reportedly been called in to assess the impact, with the attackers, scope of the attack, and whether any data was stolen currently unknown. The Air Force declined to comment on the security or operational status of the affected systems, stating that it continuously takes measures to protect its information, systems, and mission capabilities.

⚙️ Key details

Cloud One is an enterprise cloud computing platform launched in 2017 and managed by the US Air Force. It allows Department of Defense agencies to host and manage applications supporting military operations, personnel management, logistics, and maintenance.

🛡️ Related Federal Breaches

On November 21, it was revealed that hackers reportedly breached the FBI’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a nationwide database used by local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies containing information on wanted and missing persons, outstanding arrest warrants, stolen vehicles and firearms, and other criminal justice records. This intrusion followed two months after the ShinyHunters extortion group breached FBI systems by exploiting an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability in the agency’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov.

Earlier this week, hackers also reportedly breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). The incident also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA). Hours after the CIA breach was reported, the US Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it was investigating unauthorized access to its systems. It is unclear whether any of the recently disclosed federal government breaches are connected.

🧩 How it works

The CIA breach was reportedly conducted using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing platform. ARTEX is an open-source penetration testing framework that uses AI agents to automate various stages of a cyberattack, including discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities, escalating privileges, and stealing data. The framework integrates with external AI models from Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, DeepSeek, Grok, and others, allowing attackers to conduct autonomous attacks against organizations with minimal human intervention. According to the FBI, some ARTEX-powered intrusions have progressed from initial targeting to privileged access in less than three hours.

#USAirForce #CloudOne #ARTEX #FBI #Cyberattacks

Source: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach

item.title: 1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise
item.description:
1Password discloses breach after GitHub account compromise

1Password disclosed a data breach after an employee’s corporate GitHub account was hacked. The attacker used the compromised account to deploy malicious code to the company’s backend services to steal customer data.

🔍 Overview

The company began investigating the breach on November 19 after detecting indications that an employee’s GitHub account had been compromised. 1Password states that customer password vaults and the encryption keys protecting them were not compromised in the attack.

🧩 How it works

The attacker accessed private source code repositories and injected malicious code into backend services that downloaded customer account records. The malicious code also stole internal company source code and accessed the company’s continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment, potentially exposing internal infrastructure credentials.

⚙️ Key details

The following customer data was stolen in the breach:

  • Customer names and email addresses
  • Account and user IDs
  • Account creation and last sign-in timestamps
  • Public cryptographic keys
  • Secure Remote Password (SRP) protocol parameters
  • Invitation, provisioning, and account recovery tokens
  • Other internal account metadata

The stolen tokens were embedded in links that 1Password emailed to users to accept account provisioning invitations or recover their accounts. 1Password says these tokens cannot be used on their own to access customer accounts, as completing the invitation or recovery process requires either single sign-on (SSO) authentication or a six-digit verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

🚀 Availability

1Password has disabled the compromised GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked potentially exposed infrastructure credentials. The company has also hired independent cybersecurity experts to validate its remediation efforts. As a precaution against brute-force attacks, 1Password has strengthened these verification codes from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric characters. The company states that only a small number of users were affected and have been individually notified.

💡 Why it matters

While customer vaults were not compromised, the stolen data is valuable to threat actors as it provides a list of known 1Password users who could be targeted in phishing campaigns. Threat actors could send emails impersonating 1Password, using the breach as a lure to trick customers into disclosing their account passwords, Secret Keys, or recovery verification codes. 1Password is not requiring customers to change their account passwords or Secret Keys but warns them to watch for unexpected invitations, account recovery requests, and other potential phishing attempts.

#1Password #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #GitHub #Phishing

Source: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach

item.title: AI Agents Fuel Large-Scale Cyberattacks on European Critical Infrastructure
item.description:
AI Agents Fuel Large-Scale Cyberattacks on European Critical Infrastructure

Recent alerts from Swiss and Italian cybersecurity agencies confirm that autonomous AI agents are conducting large‑scale attacks on critical‑infrastructure organisations, using publicly available frameworks to find and exploit vulnerabilities quickly.

🔍 Overview

  • Swiss NCSC: first reports of AI‑assisted attacks on Swiss organisations, including critical infrastructure across at least two sectors.
  • “In recent days, the NCSC has received its first reports of cyberattacks against organisations in Switzerland in which the attack was carried out with the assistance of an AI agent,” the Swiss NCSC said.
  • Various organisations and operators of critical infrastructure across at least two sectors have been affected by these cyberattacks.
  • In all cyberattacks known to the NCSC, the use of AI agents led to the successful compromise of the victim’s IT systems.
  • Italian CSIRT Italia: detected large‑scale campaigns using autonomous AI agents on exposed endpoints; observed multiple agents working in parallel; rapid attacks exploiting weak passwords and known vulnerabilities; AI chained vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, compromised credentials.
  • The agency described rapid attacks in which agents exploited weak passwords and known vulnerabilities in exposed endpoints, using frameworks to verify weaknesses and independently decide what to do next.
  • In some cases, the agency observed multiple AI agents working in parallel to compromise a large number of systems within a few hours.
  • In one instance involving a DeepSeek Harness setup, a coordinator assigned tasks to five AI agents that undertook a broad spectrum of operational stages, from information gathering to exploitation and persistence.
  • Agents chained vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and compromised credentials, leveraging exposed systems as a foothold to reach internal networks.

🧩 How it Works

“During the observed campaigns, autonomous agents demonstrated the ability to carry out complex, sustained activity to detect misconfigurations, link even low‑impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains, and dynamically adapt their operating modules,” CSIRT Italia says.

“They went as far as writing malicious code in real time to evade endpoint defenses and carry out actions deeper within the infrastructure.”

⚙️ Key Details

Framework Involved in recent breaches and hacking incidents
ARTEX AI Yes
CyberStrikeAI Yes
DeepSeek Harness - Red Team Yes
PentAGI Yes
  • Reduce the number of systems exposed on the internet.
  • Prioritize patching, especially internet‑facing systems within 24 hours of release.
  • Add multi‑factor authentication (MFA) or passkey protection.
  • Enforce least‑privilege principles.
  • Disable remote management interfaces if not needed.
  • Monitor control‑plane operations, authentication sources, traffic to internal networks, and outbound server traffic.
  • The number of publicly available AI agents has nearly doubled since October, fueling large waves of attacks.

💡 Why it Matters

  • AI agents can rapidly identify and exploit vulnerabilities across many systems.
  • They chain low‑impact vulnerabilities into complex attack chains.
  • They can write malicious code in real time to evade defenses.
  • The attacks have already compromised IT systems in critical infrastructure.
  • Urgent mitigation is required to protect exposed assets.

#AIagents #Cybersecurity #CriticalInfrastructure #SwissNCSC #ItalianCSIRT

Source: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks

item.title: Attackers Chain Exploits to Target Exposed Palo Alto Networks Devices
item.description:
Attackers Chain Exploits to Target Exposed Palo Alto Networks Devices

Threat actors are chaining exploits for the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia vulnerabilities to target Palo Alto Networks devices with management interfaces exposed to the internet.

🧩 How it works

The attacks combine two distinct security issues:

  • PHP2Shell: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. These allow unauthenticated attackers to run code remotely with the privileges of the PHP web worker.
  • Fragnesia: A Linux kernel vulnerability in the XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem (CVE-2026-46300) that lets a local attacker with low privileges escalate permissions to root level.

A November 28 alert from CISA warned that these issues were being chained to deploy PHP webshells on vulnerable systems and execute commands as root. Dream Security researchers reported observing a campaign using this specific chain, targeting servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, including a U.S. government affiliate.

⚙️ Key details

  • Exploitation vector: Palo Alto Networks confirmed in an advisory that attacks target firewalls running PAN-OS with their management interface exposed to the public internet.
  • Exposure: The company stated that all observed exploitation activity involved devices that exposed their management interface to the public internet, contrary to recommended best practices.
  • Chaining specifics: While technical details of the chaining were not provided, Palo Alto Networks noted that the observed method is the only known way to exploit the Fragnesia flaw.

🛡️ Mitigation

  • PHP2Shell update: Administrators who already applied updates addressing the PHP2Shell flaw are considered safe from these specific chained attacks.
  • Fragnesia fixes: Fixes have been released for PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2, with the exact patch-carrying build varying by release.
  • Network configuration: For those requiring a remote management interface, Palo Alto Networks recommends restricting access to trusted internal IP addresses.

#Cybersecurity #PaloAltoNetworks #CVE #ZeroDay #SecurityVulnerability

Source: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks

item.title: Autumn-27 ARTEX Open-Source Fork Now Maintained by ChainReactors
item.description:
Autumn-27 ARTEX Open-Source Fork Now Maintained by ChainReactors

The Autumn-27/ARTEX project, an AI autonomous penetration testing system originally built with a Go backend and Next.js frontend, has seen its open-source continuation. The repository RuoJi6/ARTEX is a fork of the original Autumn-27/ARTEX, preserving the upstream commit history and AGPL-3.0 license. It is now maintained by ChainReactors.

🧩 How it works

The system integrates with external data sources to streamline asset collection. Specifically, it supports direct synchronization of asset data from ScopeSentry, eliminating the need for manual repeated collection. Users configure the ScopeSentry address and API key on the “Asset Sync” page, select targets and asset types (such as domains, subdomains, IPs, ports, sites, or endpoints) by project or task dimension, and import data to merge it into the ARTEX asset graph for agent exploration.

⚙️ Key details

  • Database & LLM: The system depends on PostgreSQL and requires an LLM configuration for exploration, supporting either ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (configurable via CLI or UI).
  • MCP Support: Remote MCP can be configured in system settings using http (Streamable HTTP) or sse (legacy SSE).
  • Dockerization: The ruoji6/artex Docker image is built and published via GitHub Actions. It includes common tools like ripgrep, curl, vim, npm, and nmap. The image supports linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 architectures, with Docker automatically selecting the matching host architecture.
  • Persistence: The ./skills and ./data directories are persisted via bind mounts.

🚀 Availability

  • Docker Setup: The installation script automatically detects and installs Docker. Users can choose between “All Docker” (which generates a .env file and runs docker compose up -d) or local compilation.
  • Local Setup: For local runs, users select a database option, generate a config.json, and compile an embedded single binary.
  • Access: After installation, the service is accessible at http://localhost:8787, requiring an initial setup at /setup to set the admin password.
  • Download: Release packages are available for download from the repository’s Releases page. Linux ARM64 users (including ARM64 Kali) should select the linux-arm64 build, while x86_64 users select linux-amd64.
  • Execution: Users must launch the application using start.sh or start.bat rather than running ./artex directly. These scripts act as daemons that restart the program based on exit codes, which is required for the “one-click update” feature to function correctly.

#ARTEX #PenetrationTesting #OpenSource #SecurityTools #ChainReactors

Source: RuoJi6/ARTEX

item.title: AWS Security Blog Launches Remediation Guides and AI Agents for Vulnerability Management
item.description:
AWS Security Blog Launches Remediation Guides and AI Agents for Vulnerability Management

AWS Security Blog released 19 October posts detailing remediation flows from security findings to tested fixes, including AI-powered guidance for finding, confirming, and repairing vulnerabilities. The posts also cover penetration testing integration into CI/CD pipelines, trusted identity propagation for AI agents, and post-quantum cryptography preparation. AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities achieved an 89.0 percent end-to-end success rate on the CyberGym-E2E benchmark, while AWS Continuum for penetration testing confirmed 33 of 37 recent CVEs with an 89.2 percent success rate. New Amazon GuardDuty Extended Threat Detection indicators include vulnerability, malicious package, reachability, misconfiguration, and sensitive data. AWS Threat Intelligence detected PHP2Shell vulnerability activity four days before public disclosure, emphasizing the need for hour-level patching of internet-facing systems. The Cybersecurity Awareness Month series highlights career paths into security, including roles in risk measurement, detection tool building, and space infrastructure security.

#AWS #AI #Security #Vulnerability #PenetrationTesting

Source: ICYMI: October 2026 @AWS Security | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Remus Infostealer Uses Malicious Chrome Extension to Harvest Gmail Emails
item.description:
Remus Infostealer Uses Malicious Chrome Extension to Harvest Gmail Emails

The Remus infostealer was found to exfiltrate Gmail messages using a stealthy malicious Chrome extension, a capability the operators advertised as a zero‑day exploit in Google’s email service.

🔍 Overview

  • On November 8 the developer began advertising an alleged Gmail zero‑day that could collect emails even after password changes and session revocations.
  • Hudson Rock’s investigation was inconclusive; however, customer evidence matched the seller’s claim despite no technical proof of a zero‑day.

🧩 How it works

  • A native DLL loads the extension into Google Chrome; Chrome is the only targeted browser.
  • The DLL contains the extension as an unencrypted ZIP archive in its .rdata section.
  • Because Chrome 137+ removed the command‑line option for loading extensions, Remus edits the victim’s Chrome profile, registers the extension, and enables Developer Mode to run it as an unpacked extension.
  • The extension masquerades as “Google Sheets”, copies the description of Google Docs Offline, and requests permission to access all websites.

⚙️ Technical details

Attribute Detail
Name Google Sheets
Fake description Copies description of Google Docs Offline
Permissions requested Access to all websites
  • Once active, it checks for unread emails every minute across up to 10 Gmail account slots and retrieves them in raw format.
  • It sends the email subject, body, sender, and victim’s email address plus a campaign identifier to its command‑and‑control server.
  • Failed uploads are queued and retried; a local record prevents duplicate exfiltration.
  • The extension also parses attachment filenames but does not forward them, indicating incomplete implementation.

🛡️ Mitigation

  • Install software only from trusted sources.
  • Regularly review chrome://extensions for unexpected entries or Developer Mode activation.

#Remus #ChromeExtension #Infostealer #Gmail

Source: Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension

item.title: AI-Driven Cyberattacks Shift from Theory to Real-World Execution
item.description:
AI-Driven Cyberattacks Shift from Theory to Real-World Execution

AI-driven attacks are on the rise, transitioning from theoretical risks to real-world threats. Recent investigations reveal that criminals are using AI to accelerate attacks at scale, with attackers leveraging AI agents to execute context-aware commands with real-time decision-making.

🔍 Overview

In one observed campaign, a highly persistent threat actor utilized AI to generate 117 unique scripts across multiple languages and executed over 8,000 unique commands in just 12 days. This volume significantly exceeds the capabilities of normal attackers, who usually execute dozens of commands with a few scripts over similar periods.

⚙️ Key Details

The observed attack campaign featured two distinct phases, characterized by different execution styles:

Phase Characteristics Execution Metrics
Human Attacker Made typographical errors, repeated manual checks, demonstrated environment confusion Median time between commands roughly 24 seconds
Agentic Phase Flawless, zero-syntax-error commands Median gap between commands just 1.4 seconds

When instructed to execute aspects of an attack, the AI agent rapidly scans networks, attempts to elevate privileges, and utilizes legitimate native tools to blend in.

💡 Why It Matters

Attack isolation and near real-time response are now critical mandates. If defenders wait hours to react, an AI agent can already have enumerated cloud infrastructure and extracted or encrypted data. To effectively defend against these threats, defenders must employ AI-powered tools.

Leveraging AI on the edge—specifically on endpoints and Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFW)—is a major strategic necessity. Edge-based AI can process telemetry instantly, making split-second decisions to terminate malicious web shell sessions or block active privilege escalation attempts locally. In observed product deployments, edge AI operated in milliseconds rather than the minutes required by agentic LLMs.

Furthermore, local edge AI maintains detection coverage even if an attack vector is used to temporarily disable network traffic to operate silently. This approach enables defenders to catch and isolate threats at the earliest possible stage and safeguards sensitive corporate data locally without requiring telemetry or proprietary data to be transmitted to the cloud for analysis.

🧩 Defense Strategy

Despite their speed, agentic AI attackers have a foundational weakness: they enter the environment without information. Defenders hold an upper hand through comprehensive AI analytics.

  • Data Normalization: Collecting telemetry across diverse network, endpoint, identity, and cloud sources to map distinct data streams into a single, cohesive schema.
  • Advanced Stitching: Merging related events across disparate sensors into unified, context-rich stories rather than disconnected events.
  • Baseline Establishment: AI analytics engines make it easier to create and update baselines.
  • Automated Response: Organizations must combine real-time detection with automated response capabilities, enabling instant attack isolation and automated remediation before critical systems or data are compromised.

#Cybersecurity #AIAgents #EdgeAI #ThreatDetection #NetworkSecurity

Source: The AI Threat Horizon: Why Speed, Edge AI and Baselines Are Our Best Defense

item.title: AWS Network Firewall Adds Context-Aware Rules and Next Generation Policies
item.description:
AWS Network Firewall Adds Context-Aware Rules and Next Generation Policies

AWS Network Firewall has updated its capabilities to support context-aware rules, allowing you to match traffic based on the AWS resources that send and receive it rather than by their IP addresses. Alongside this, AWS has introduced Next Generation policies, which separate access control and threat protection into independent engines to help simplify firewall management and policy scaling.

🔍 Overview

Rules that match on IP addresses must keep up with every workload that scales out, is replaced, or moves. Short-lived workloads are the hardest to keep up with; for example, a VPC-attached AWS Lambda function can scale out and start sending traffic before an updated IP list reaches the firewall. Context-aware rules solve this issue by allowing you to filter a function’s traffic by the security group attached to it, or by naming a virtual private cloud (VPC), a subnet, or a transit gateway attachment.

🧩 How it works

Context-aware rules require transit gateway-attached firewalls and function by combining a control path and a data path:

  • The Control Path: A context store—which is a catalog of the AWS resources that can send and receive traffic through a transit gateway—tells the firewall which resources exist. You create this in AWS Network Manager and associate it with the transit gateway that your firewall uses.
  • The Data Path: The transit gateway adds the context of the sender (including its VPC, subnet, transit gateway attachment, and security groups) to each packet.
  • The Firewall Engine: The firewall receives these two paths, reads the context on each packet, and matches it against your configured rules. Source context works with every protocol, while destination context requires TCP-based rules because the firewall learns the receiving resource from return traffic.

Here is how context rules apply to specific AWS resources:

Resource Type Rule Application
Subnet or VPC Applies to each new resource that you launch in it.
Security Group Applies to each new resource whose network interface has that security group attached.
Transit Gateway Attachment Applies to traffic that enters through that attachment.

⚙️ Next Generation Policies

In a Classic policy, your access rules and threat rules run together in a single stateful engine and share one rule capacity. With Next Generation policies, access control and threat protection each get their own stateful engine in the same firewall, executed in sequence:

  1. Firewall Engine: This engine handles access control and is drop by default. Built on Suricata 8 firewall mode, it follows each connection through its entire flow (including the TCP handshake and TLS client hello) and evaluates rules along the way up to the application layer.
  2. IPS Engine: This engine manages threat protection and is pass by default. Traffic allowed by the firewall engine moves here, where the IPS engine checks it using AWS managed rule groups or custom rules that you write.

Because each engine has its own rule capacity, adding access rules does not take capacity away from threat protection. This design allows networking and security teams to work independently on their own configurations without risk of overwriting each other’s rules.

#AWS #NetworkFirewall #CloudSecurity #VPC #TransitGateway

Source: Introducing context-aware rules for AWS Network Firewall | Amazon Web Services Source: Introducing AWS Network Firewall Next Generation policy | Amazon Web Services

item.title: CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework
item.description:
CIA and FinCEN Report Cyberattacks Using ARTEX Framework

Unknown attackers breached an open-source intelligence (OSINT) analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and also affected the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency. Additionally, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed an investigation into unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.

🔍 Overview

  • The cyberattack was reportedly carried out using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.
  • The incident affected the CIA, the ODNI, and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency.
  • FinCEN is a US Department of the Treasury bureau that acts as the country’s official Financial Intelligence Unit and protects the nation’s financial system from illicit activities.

⚙️ Key details

  • The CIA and ODNI have not yet replied to a request for more details regarding the incident.
  • No classified data or systems were exposed in the breach.
  • A source stated, “The hack did not involve our classified networks or classified information, and no other systems are currently at risk.”
  • After detecting the attack, FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution and told banks to use the Financial Institutions Hotline to file reports, since some services may be unavailable.
  • It is unclear how the attackers gained access, when the breach occurred, or whether they stole any information from the compromised systems.

💡 Why it matters

  • These incidents follow a series of other cyberattacks that have led to security breaches at other US federal agencies in recent years.
  • One week ago, the US National Security Agency’s classified network suffered a days-long outage, which the agency attributed to scheduled routine maintenance.
  • Two years ago, the Silk Typhoon Chinese state-backed hacking group breached the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), the Treasury’s Office of Financial Research, and the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.
  • Hackers reportedly breached the FBI’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC).
  • The ShinyHunters extortion group claimed it breached the FBI’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, prompting an FBI investigation that led to the arrests of multiple suspected members.

#cybersecurity #CIA #FinCEN #AI #databreach

Source: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system

item.title: CISA Warns of Critical Vulnerability in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers
item.description:
CISA Warns of Critical Vulnerability in Danfoss Refrigeration Controllers

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is warning about a critical vulnerability in Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controllers, which are used by food retailers to manage commercial refrigeration, HVAC, and lighting systems.

🔍 Overview

The security issue is tracked as CVE-2026-129713 and received a severity score of 9.8. It is identified as a stack-based buffer overflow in the controller’s server. CISA notes that an attacker can trigger the flaw without authentication, cause the server to restart, and potentially achieve remote code execution with the web server’s privileges.

These controllers have been compromised recently in attacks at various supermarkets and food retailers across Europe, where hackers remotely shut down cooling systems or raised their temperatures.

⚙️ Key Details

The Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers serve as central control units for supermarket and convenience-store refrigeration. They are used to manage equipment such as refrigerated display cases and compressor racks, to log temperatures, and to alert when changes occur. Danfoss refers to this product line as the AK-SM 800A Series.

Model Description
820A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series
850A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series
880A Part of the AK-SM 800A Series

Depending on the model, these units can also control store lighting and HVAC. While CISA notes that the controllers are deployed worldwide, their exact number remains unclear.

🛡️ Recent Attacks

  • On October 11 and 12, several French supermarkets and food retailers suffered significant losses after attacks attributed to Iran’s IRGC-linked Shahid Kaveh unit. The attackers compromised Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC and Copeland/Dixell XWEB refrigeration controllers, remotely altering defrost settings.
  • On November 2, at least 115 supermarket stores in Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Romania, and Estonia had their refrigeration equipment shut down or their settings changed remotely.
  • Supplier Sabcobel stated that the attackers used the same vulnerability previously seen in the October attacks in France, indicating Danfoss systems were involved again.
  • Also on November 2, attackers suspected to be linked to the same campaign targeted a refrigeration supplier for the French national blood service, altering cold-storage settings at three facilities.

🚀 Availability

There is currently no patch available for CVE-2026-129713. On November 20, Danfoss published a security advisory stating that the vulnerability would be addressed in the upcoming software version 5.5.x for the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series. The company also said the update would remove the option that allows customers to turn off ‘Strict mode’ in the product.

💡 Why It Matters

In the absence of a patch, system administrators are advised to take the following actions:

  • Keep controllers off of the public internet and minimize network exposure where possible.
  • Segregate control systems from business networks and place them behind firewalls.
  • Use up-to-date Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) when remote access is required.

#CISA #CVE-2026-129713 #Danfoss #SupplyChain #OTSecurity

Source: CISA warns of critical unpatched flaw in Danfoss refrigeration controllers

item.title: Eclypsium Report: Most Infrastructure Security Fixes Address Bundled Software Flaws
item.description:
Eclypsium Report: Most Infrastructure Security Fixes Address Bundled Software Flaws

Eclypsium’s November InfraTrust Pulse report indicates that the majority of infrastructure security advisories addressing exploited vulnerabilities over the past month involve flaws in third-party software bundled into products rather than code developed by the vendors themselves.

🔍 Overview

The report tracks 373 new security advisories published by 23 infrastructure vendors between October 15 and November 19, covering 3,880 vulnerabilities. Of these advisories, 98 were rated critical, and 38 contained vulnerabilities listed in CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. However, 33 of those 38 advisories fixed exploited flaws in bundled software components, primarily PHP, Node.js, and OpenSSH.

⚙️ Key Details

These vulnerabilities pose additional risks for enterprises because, even after a software developer releases a security fix, organizations must wait for infrastructure vendors to incorporate it into their products. “Your exposure to exploited flaws depends on how quickly each vendor rebuilds its products after an upstream fix ships,” the report reads. As of November 20, PHP2Shell fixes were either partially available or had yet to be released for affected products from Fortinet, Juniper, Lenovo, HPE, Netgear, HP, and Siemens. The November 19 release of another 18 PHP security advisories further complicated patching efforts for infrastructure vendors and their customers.

🚨 Active Exploitations

Threat actors are chaining PHP vulnerabilities with other flaws to gain root access to compromised devices. An example is the two PHP vulnerabilities known as PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) highlighted in last month’s InfraTrust report, which are now being exploited in attacks against Palo Alto Networks and Check Point firewalls. Check Point reported that destructive attacks deployed data-wiping malware on VMware ESXi hosts. Other notable active exploits include:

  • Cisco Expressway: CVE-2026-76466, a critical vulnerability added to CISA’s KEV catalog on November 20. On November 23, CISA flagged this flaw as actively exploited after Russian cybersecurity firm F6 spotted hackers using it to gain root privileges.
  • Palo Alto Networks and Check Point: The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities and CVE-2026-123039 in Check Point gateways. Check Point warned that this flaw was being actively exploited to gain root privileges and establish persistence on vulnerable devices since late October.
  • Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator: CVE-2026-114625, a critical vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.9 that was exploited in zero-day attacks.
  • Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD: CVE-2026-76418, affecting devices configured for remote-access VPNs. The flaw was exploited in attacks to crash devices.
  • SonicWall SonicOS: CVE-2026-19868, allowing multifactor authentication bypass on VPNs configured with single sign-on. SonicWall warned that it received reports that the flaw was exploited in zero-day attacks.

💡 Recommendations

Administrators should also prioritize installing Fortinet’s October hardening updates, which addressed numerous vulnerabilities discovered using AI models. As AI makes it easier to discover and exploit vulnerabilities, InfraTrust warns that organizations must take additional steps to protect their devices while waiting for vendors to release security updates. These include:

  • Removing management interfaces from the Internet
  • Segmenting them internally to limit lateral movement
  • Investigating previously exposed devices for backdoors that may remain even after security updates are installed

“Patching is table stakes, but what you do before the patch is available and after the exploit hits will determine whether you survive,” the report concludes.

#Cybersecurity #Infrastructure #SupplyChain #VulnerabilityManagement #PatchManagement

Source: InfraTrust warns of exploited supply chain flaws in network appliances

item.title: Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware
item.description:
Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware

Cybersecurity company Radware experienced a data breach after an unauthorized party accessed an unauthenticated internal Cloud WAF management API left reachable from the public internet on November 19, 2026.

🔍 Incident Overview

Radware detected the unauthorized access on a Thursday, ten hours after the initial intrusion. Upon detection, the company took several immediate response actions:

  • Blocked the originating IP address and disabled public access to the internal management API.
  • Revoked and replaced all internal account credentials.
  • Initiated a root cause analysis report, which was later shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer.

Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.

⚙️ Impacted Systems and Data

The exposure was limited to specific account management details and log export configurations, while core traffic inspection remained unaffected.

System / Data Category Status According to Radware
Customer contact details Potentially accessed
Log export credentials (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, SFTP) Potentially accessed for a subset of customers
WAF traffic inspection and certificates Not exposed
End-users’ data and customer application traffic Not exposed
Cloud DDoS services and data Not exposed

Radware stated that WAF traffic inspection and protection have continued without interruption, with no evidence found of policy changes or access to customer application traffic.

💡 Customer Action Advised

Radware strongly advised affected AppSec (WAF, BOT) customers to take immediate remedial steps:

  • Rotate exposed Cloud WAF log export credentials, including Azure Blob Storage keys or SAS tokens, AWS S3 access keys, or SFTP credentials, as soon as possible.
  • Review access logs on cloud storage accounts for unexpected access dating back to at least November 19.

The company noted it has already received reports from customers regarding AWS alerts for an unfamiliar IP address attempting to access their log-export buckets.

📊 Investigation and Public Response

Radware is continuing to investigate the incident to determine whether any exposed API keys or customer information were used without authorization. As of the report, Radware has not issued a public statement, filed a breach report with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, or provided an immediate response to inquiries from BleepingComputer.

#Cybersecurity #DataBreach #Radware #CloudSecurity #APISecurity

Source: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys

item.title: New Extortion Group Inception Targets SSO Credentials; ShinyHunters Claims Return
item.description:
New Extortion Group Inception Targets SSO Credentials; ShinyHunters Claims Return

🕵️ Inception Targets Global Brands

A newly formed data extortion group named ‘Inception’ has been linked to a large-scale campaign targeting single sign-on (SSO) credentials of multiple global brands. The gang surfaced on November 17, claiming seven victims on its extortion site, including chip maker AMD, PepsiCo, Cigna Healthcare, AutoZone, and Lucid Motors. However, none of these companies have publicly confirmed a data breach.

Cybersecurity company ReversingLabs has tracked the group’s activity since late October, identifying an extensive infrastructure that includes 21 domains used for SSO phishing, 41 domains believed to be part of the campaign infrastructure, and 4 other domains with suspected use. This infrastructure impersonates dozens of major corporations, including Dropbox, Duolingo, Western Union, Indeed, Activision Blizzard, Riot Games, Twitch, Reddit, Nestlé, Anthropic, Nintendo, Starbucks, McDonald’s, Paramount, and NBCUniversal. The existence of these domains does not prove those firms have been breached or targeted yet.

⚙️ Tactics and Infrastructure

The Inception campaign appears to rely on phone-based social engineering rather than email phishing, strongly resembling tactics used by the ShinyHunters extortion group. The actors use legal-themed websites that imitate corporate authentication services, primarily Okta but also NetIQ/OpenText Access Manager.

Component Details
Phishing Domains 21 domains identified by ReversingLabs
Infrastructure Domains 41 domains believed to be used in the campaign
Suspected Domains 4 additional domains with suspected use
Impersonated Brands Includes Dropbox, Duolingo, Western Union, and Nintendo
Authentication Services Okta, NetIQ/OpenText Access Manager

Okta published a report linking Inception to threat cluster O-UNC-053, which was previously associated with ShinyHunters and active since March. According to Okta, after law enforcement disrupted ShinyHunters, O-UNC-053 continued to register new phishing domains. In late October, the cluster launched a legal-themed campaign, and in mid-November, the Inception leak site went live. Okta assessed that the cluster very likely changed its brand affiliation, maintaining consistent infrastructure and TTPs.

Inception responded to these links by claiming on its extortion page that it operates independently and has no affiliation to previous groups. The actors argued that overlapping targets and common domain registration services do not establish operational links, noting that private tooling circulates among independent threat actors.

📢 ShinyHunters Reemerges

Following a series of arrests targeting alleged ShinyHunters members, the group claimed to have returned on November 23 via a new Tor site. The site contains messages in Russian and English announcing the group’s return and distancing itself from alleged impostors. The operators denounced a former member, reportedly arrested and cooperating with law enforcement, and mocked other individuals tied to the investigation, including Umbreon and Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky.

To verify their identity, the new operators published two verification messages signed using historical ShinyHunters PGP keys dating back to 2020. BleepingComputer confirmed that both messages were signed using known PGP keys associated with the group, indicating access to the private signing keys. However, these keys do not confirm that the individuals behind the new operation are the same people who previously controlled the group, as the keys have circulated among numerous people. The operators stated they plan to launch a new CDN for hosting stolen data and will communicate exclusively through a specific Exploit hacking forum account and the new Tor site.

🛡️ Defending Against the Threat

ReversingLabs recommends enforcing phishing-resistant authentication, including FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and strengthening help desk identity verification procedures to defend against the Inception campaign. Security teams should carefully review DNS, proxy, and identity provider logs dating back to October 21, 2026, for signs of suspicious activity.

#ShinyHunters #Inception #SSO #DataExtortion #Phishing #Okta

Source: New Inception extortion gang launches large-scale vishing campaign Source: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof

item.title: Rackspace to Shut Down Spot Platform After Security Breach
item.description:
Rackspace to Shut Down Spot Platform After Security Breach

Rackspace is shutting down its Rackspace Spot cloud platform, which allows organizations to deploy and manage containerized applications using Kubernetes, following a security breach that allowed hackers to access customer clusters and secrets. Customers are given until December 8 to migrate their services and download their data before the platform is permanently discontinued.

🚨 The Breach and Discovery

The decision to discontinue the service comes after a security incident that occurred on November 17, when hackers breached Rackspace Spot using compromised credentials. The intrusion allowed unauthorized actors to create pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and list nodes and volumes. Rackspace discovered the intrusion on November 18 following a customer report and subsequently disabled access to the platform’s administration console to secure its infrastructure.

The service was restored on November 21 following an extended outage. Rackspace stated that the affected Spot environment is segmented from its core infrastructure and that it has not identified evidence of unauthorized access to its core systems or the environments of other Rackspace customers.

⚙️ Customer Instructions and Indicators of Compromise

Rackspace has instructed all Spot customers to treat their API tokens, refresh tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes Secrets as potentially compromised, regardless of whether they previously received a breach notification. Customers are also advised to review access logs dating back to November 16 and search for suspicious Kubernetes objects associated with the attack.

The following indicators of compromise have been provided for customers to search within their logs:

Indicator Type Details
IP Address 23.224.79.106
IP Range 23.224.0.0/15
Suspicious Kubernetes Pod and Object Prefixes i1, glm-, and probe

📅 Shutdown Details

Rackspace announced the shutdown in a new security notification, stating it had decided to wind down the Rackspace Spot service to provide a clear path forward for customers. The service will be permanently discontinued on December 8, 2026, at 5 PM Central Time, at which point all remaining workloads will be terminated and customer data will no longer be accessible. Customers are instructed to retrieve their data and migrate their workloads to different platforms before this deadline.

💡 Customer Response

The shutdown announcement has prompted disappointment among Rackspace Spot customers, with some urging the company to reconsider and offering to pay more to keep the platform operational. In a Reddit discussion, one customer said they believed users would be willing to pay higher prices to keep the service running. Other customers expressed concerns about affordable alternatives and the impact the shutdown would have on their existing infrastructure, while others praised the service for its affordability. Rackspace has not indicated whether it will reconsider the shutdown decision or offer customers additional time to migrate their workloads.

#Rackspace #Security #Kubernetes #Cloud #DataBreach

Source: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach
