item.title: Amazon Bedrock Launches Trusted Access Program API and Anthropic Enterprise Safeguards
item.description:
Amazon Bedrock Launches Trusted Access Program API and Anthropic Enterprise Safeguards

Amazon Web Services has announced the general availability of the trusted access program API on Amazon Bedrock, along with the public preview of two new security-focused offerings developed in partnership with Anthropic. The API provides a centralized way for users to discover, request, and enroll in model provider trusted access programs.

🔍 Overview

The new trusted access program API on Amazon Bedrock enables developers to manage access to enterprise-grade AI models through a unified interface. The first two offerings now in public preview are Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC), which can be used with Claude Fable, Claude Mythos, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5.5 via the Cyber Verification Program (CVP).

🧩 How it works

Administrators control enrollment using existing IAM policies and service control policies. The system integrates with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) and Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), accessing encrypted data through user-defined key and bucket policies. Users can revoke access at any time, but affected models stop serving within 24 hours of access loss.

⚙️ Key details

  • EFS and EDC were built in partnership between AWS and Anthropic
  • EFS: Customer data stored in their own AWS account; prompts and completions not retained by Anthropic or Amazon Bedrock
  • EDC: Data stored in Amazon-managed storage; prompts and completions not retained by Anthropic
  • Only automated safety monitoring within AWS reads retained inputs and outputs
  • AWS human reviewers do not review content for EFS
  • Bedrock writes prompts and responses to retention and key services, encrypted with user’s KMS key or to their S3 bucket
  • Data is written to S3 within minutes; retry attempts allowed up to 72 hours for certain failures
  • Automated safety monitoring scans data for misuse and creates risk cases in user buckets when needed

🚀 Availability

The trusted access program API is generally available. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC) are available in public preview on Amazon Bedrock.

#AWS #AmazonBedrock #AISecurity #Anthropic #EnterpriseAI #MachineLearning

Source: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Analysis of 5,400 Malicious NPM Packages Reveals Evolving Supply Chain Tactics
item.description:
Analysis of 5,400 Malicious NPM Packages Reveals Evolving Supply Chain Tactics

In this first part, we analyzed approximately 5,400 confirmed malicious npm packages published between December 2025 and October 2026, the first year following npm’s revocation of long-lived authentication tokens. The dataset comprises packages detected by a scanner that analyzes npm publish events for suspicious packages, with results filtered for precision by retaining only packages with at least one independent source, such as a public advisory, a vendor-published campaign report, an npm security takedown, or analyst review. Time is measured by npm publish date, and the unit of record is the package version, dated by its first malicious version.

🔍 Threat Landscape Overview

Monthly counts of confirmed malicious packages vary by a factor of fifteen across the period. Activity remains stable with several hundred new publisher accounts per month and a flat rate of malicious packages relative to total packages published. In August 2026, a single dependency-confusion campaign accounts for 78% of confirmed versions. Dependency-confusion reconnaissance is continuous, present in every month at a consistent level, while compromise of legitimate packages is episodic.

🧩 Attack Vectors and Campaigns

Three waves of a single worm family occurred in May, June, and August 2026. The May and August waves each compromised more than one hundred packages, and the June wave republished a vendor’s entire scope in one day.

  • Token Theft Shift: Classic long-lived tokens were revoked on December 9, 2025. Theft of npm authentication tokens peaked at 22% of packages in March 2026 and fell below 5% from May. The tokens targeted in this period were plausibly granular access tokens and CI secrets.
  • Obfuscation: The share of actors whose packages trigger an obfuscation rule more than doubled between May and August 2026. 72% of packages have an obfuscation marker, and 30% retrieve a second stage.
  • Compromised Packages: 78% of compromised versions add or modify a lifecycle script, compared with 4% of attacker-created packages. 23% show a change of maintainer or publisher, but the majority of compromises are published through the legitimate account and leave ownership records unchanged.

⚙️ Attacker Profile and Package Characteristics

99% of malicious packages are published by single-maintainer accounts, and 55% of accounts use a free-mail address. Two-thirds of accounts publish exactly one malicious package; among those publishing more than one, the median interval from first to last malicious publish is under one day.

  • DPRK-nexus Campaigns: These are the exception, operating several hundred accounts at one to two packages each, with 83% on free-mail addresses.
  • Other Named Campaigns: These use free-mail addresses in 15% of cases, consistent with procured account pools.
  • Package Traits: 88% of packages are under thirty days old at the malicious publish, 75% declare no repository, and 65% retain npm init template values in the author, description, or repository fields. 54% declare a lifecycle script, and 17% carry an internal-looking name (core, utils, sdk, config). Typosquatting is a minority tactic, with 13% embedding a popular package name and under 5% being within two character edits of one.

💡 Payload Behavior and Targeting

Credential and data theft is the predominant behavior in every month, except August. In August, a significant number of packages stole credentials but ultimately aimed to deliver a Sliver command-and-control implant on the victim machine, changing their classification to Trojan / Downloader.

  • Credential Targets: 45% of credential stealers target a single credential class, while 36% target three or more. Single-class stealers are distributed evenly across cloud credentials, SSH keys, AI-developer credentials, npm tokens, and .env files. In multi-class stealers, cloud credentials, SSH keys, and .env files co-occur; wallet and browser-data theft occur separately.
  • AI Developer Credentials: Targeting remained at 1-4% of packages throughout the year, but absolute counts rose with volume. AI-developer credentials are the most specialized target: 80% of packages that target them target no other class.
  • OS Specificity: 55% of packages contain no operating-system-specific code. Droppers target Windows (PowerShell, scheduled tasks, executables), while credential stealers and backdoors target Linux (systemd, cron, shell configuration files). macOS-specific code appears in approximately one in eight stealers.
  • Scoped Packages: 24% of packages are scoped, across more than three hundred distinct scopes, most of which contain a single malicious package.

#npmSecurity #SupplyChainAttack #MalwareAnalysis #ThreatIntelligence #OpenSource

Source: What 5,400 Malicious npm Packages Reveal about Software Supply Chain Risk in 2026

item.title: Attackers Weaponize Autonomous AI Agents in 10 Global Campaigns
item.description:
Attackers Weaponize Autonomous AI Agents in 10 Global Campaigns

Attackers are weaponizing autonomous AI agents in real-world campaigns, creating a risk that until recently has only been theoretical. Between July and September 2026, more than 10 global campaigns were identified and tracked in which different attackers deployed autonomous AI agents to enhance their attacks.

🔍 Overview

These agentic AI attackers operated at machine speed, compressing the attack lifecycle from weeks or days into mere hours. The campaigns targeted diverse sectors, including government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture, and education.

In every observed campaign, attackers gained their initial foothold through web shells that were deployed via vulnerable web applications. The novelty of these agentic campaigns was not in their techniques, but in their speed and efficiency. The AI-driven operators matched the tradecraft of proficient human attackers while operating at machine scale, at times executing hundreds of unique commands in just minutes.

🧩 How It Works

An agentic AI attacker is an autonomous AI system—usually a large language model (LLM) with tool-calling capabilities—that independently plans, executes, and adapts attack sequences without continuous human guidance. Unlike chatbots that respond to individual prompts, agentic AI systems operate in a loop: they observe their environment, reason about what to do next, take action, and then observe the results to inform their next step.

The typical operational flow includes:

  • Human sets the objective: The human operator identifies a target and provides initial access, typically a web shell on a vulnerable web application.
  • AI agent takes over: The AI agent autonomously performs further reconnaissance, credential harvesting, privilege escalation, and lateral movement.
  • AI agent reports back: The AI agent structures its findings using machine-readable output formatting and periodically checks in with orchestration APIs.
  • Human makes strategic decisions: The human operator reviews the AI agent’s findings and directs high-level strategy, such as instructing the agent to target the payment system or establish persistence.
  • AI agent executes: The AI agent carries out the human’s strategic directives with tactical autonomy.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Speed and scale: An agentic AI attacker operates at machine speed. In the observed campaigns, AI agents executed hundreds of unique commands within minutes.
  • Lowered barrier to entry: Attackers can provide high-level guidance while the AI agent automates intricate technical phases, including compiling kernel exploits, navigating cross-platform lateral movement, and systematically compromising cloud infrastructure.
  • Adaptive reasoning: Unlike script-based attacks that fail when they encounter unexpected conditions, agentic AI attackers employ reasoning to try alternative approaches when failures occur. Agents were observed attempting five different privilege escalation techniques in sequence when earlier ones failed, and compiling custom exploit code on-target when pre-built binaries didn’t work.
  • Cross-domain fluency: A single agentic AI attacker can operate across Linux, Windows, various cloud platforms, web applications, databases, and network infrastructures.
  • Behavioral fingerprints: Using AI agents came at the expense of operational stealth. The agents left unmistakable behavioral fingerprints that revealed the involvement of non-human operators, including:
    • Structured machine-readable output formats.
    • Adaptive exploit selection.
    • Iterative refinement.
    • Chain-of-thought reasoning comments that appeared in shell commands.

💡 Why It Matters

New challenges in threat attribution have emerged because AI agents generate unique, dynamic payloads on the fly without distinct behavioral fingerprints, making it increasingly difficult to attribute attacks to specific threat actors.

Unit 42 AI Security Assessment service can help identify and mitigate complex AI-enabled risks. Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense is an offensive security service designed to assist organizations with continuously discovering hidden and unknown exposures in dynamic environments, validate real-world exploitability across attack paths through agentic testing and expert analysis, and provide prioritized remediation and virtual patching guidance to accelerate risk mitigation.

#Cybersecurity #AIAgents #ThreatIntelligence #PaloAltoNetworks #Unit42

Source: Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks

item.title: European Commission confirms data breach via AI-assisted attack
item.description:
European Commission confirms data breach via AI-assisted attack

The European Commission has confirmed that attackers breached its EU Academy online learning hub and stole the personal data of an undisclosed number of users. This incident follows a disclosure that hackers breached the Commission’s systems on October 22 using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.

🔍 Overview

  • The attack was conducted using the ARTEX AI-powered penetration testing framework.
  • The breach affected the EU Academy platform, which is used to learn about EU policies and follow EU online courses.
  • The incident caused service disruptions that also affected the internal Sysper HR platform.
  • The Commission stated it has not detected evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole.
  • No ransom demands have been received, and the attack has not yet been attributed to a specific actor.

🚨 Key details

  • Stolen data included users’ personal information, such as names and email addresses.
  • As a protective measure, the Commission temporarily took down several applications, most of which have since been restored.
  • Public access to the EU Academy platform has been disabled.
  • Users on the platform received a message warning them to be suspicious of unsolicited emails or messages that may be part of potential phishing attacks.
  • The investigation into the incident is still ongoing.

⚙️ Broader context

  • In February, the Commission disclosed a data breach after discovering on January 30 that a mobile device management platform used for staff devices had been compromised.
  • On March 27, the Commission disclosed an additional incident following a breach of its Amazon cloud environment.
  • The EU’s Cybersecurity Service (CERT-EU) attributed the March cloud hack to the TeamPCP threat group, noting it exposed the data of at least 29 other Union entities.
  • These incidents follow the Commission’s January 20 proposal for new cybersecurity legislation aimed at strengthening defenses against cybercrime groups and state-backed actors.

#EuropeanCommission #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #Artemis #AIHacking

Source: European Commission confirms data theft in EU Academy breach

item.title: KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals
item.description:
KEPCO Data Breach Exposes 1.5 Million Individuals

A threat actor breached the internal network of Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), exposing details of more than 1.5 million individuals.

🔍 Overview

  • KEPCO, South Korea’s main electric power company, detected an attack on November 20.
  • The breach exposed customer, employee, and contractor data.
  • The attack was detected when unauthorized access was confirmed to KEPCO ON and SRM systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • The following data was exposed:
    • For 650,487 KEPCO ON customers: names, ID information, phone numbers, addresses, bank names, bank account numbers, account holder names, card issuers, card numbers, cardholder names, and electricity charge and billing information.
    • For 426,827 company representatives: names, ID information, email addresses, and company addresses.
    • For 442,934 KEPCO employees: names, affiliation, employee ID number, mobile phone number, email address, company phone number.
  • The data breach resulted from “advanced technologies as AI,” but specific details about the initial access method or attack chain were not shared.
  • KEPCO is notifying exposed individuals directly, has filed a report with the data protection authorities, and is coordinating with government and financial authorities to block abuse.

💡 Why it matters

  • Potentially exposed individuals are warned that the exposed information could be used for targeted phishing and impersonation.
  • They are advised to report any attempts to the police or Korea’s Internet and Security Agency.
  • It is recommended to avoid installing unknown apps, entering information into suspicious forms, and sharing sensitive data or verification codes over calls or texts.

🔗 Attribution

  • A threat actor using the “Noiem” alias has claimed the attack and advertised the breach on a hacker forum on November 19.
  • South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission separately confirmed that KEPCO received an email from a hacker claiming data theft on November 19.
  • While these claims match the available evidence, attribution to Noiem remains unconfirmed.

#KEPCO #DataBreach #CyberSecurity #SouthKorea #CriticalInfrastructure

Source: South Korea’s power giant KEPCO confirms data breach impacting 1.5 million

item.title: McDonald's Japan Confirms Data Breach via Smartphone App Database Access
item.description:
McDonald’s Japan Confirms Data Breach via Smartphone App Database Access

McDonald’s Japan has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company’s official smartphone app. The exposed information includes users’ product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs. The company confirmed that the exposed data does not include names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or credit card information. A follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of official apps as a result of the incident. McDonald’s Japan is working to invalidate any credentials used for unauthorized access, investigate the relevant systems, and report to the Personal Information Protection Commission. This is not the first data breach to affect McDonald’s in recent years, with the fast food giant disclosing a breach in June 2021 after attackers breached its systems and stole information belonging to employees and customers from the US, South Korea, and Taiwan. In 2017, McDonald’s also patched a cross-site scripting (XSS) security flaw that affected its official website and exposed customers’ plain-text passwords. Last month, Burger King Japan also disclosed a major data breach after attackers stole 11.18 million customer records that were later leaked online. The two incidents affecting the two Japanese fast food chains add to a large wave of cyberattacks impacting high-profile Japanese companies since the start of the year, including Japan Airlines, entertainment system maker Daiichi Kosho, cloud and digital infrastructure firm IDC Frontier, Japanese publishing giant Nikkei, cloud and data center service provider Sakura Internet, taxi operator Nihon Kotsu, telecommunications giant KDDI, and many others. Macnica researcher Yutaka Sejiyama has logged 288 cybersecurity incidents affecting Japanese organizations involving personal information theft or exposure since the start of the year. Sejiyama found that attackers are now probing websites and APIs for access-control, configuration, and authentication weaknesses, and exploiting known (n-day) vulnerabilities to find other victims.

#databreaches #cybersecurity #mcdonalds #japan #dataprotection #infosec

Source: McDonald’s Japan data breach exposes customer location information

item.title: OpenAI and Cisco Launch Open-Source Shirudo Security Tool
item.description:
OpenAI and Cisco Launch Open-Source Shirudo Security Tool

OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo. The tool deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, allowing operators to do so without restarting services.

🧩 How it works

Shirudo leverages the eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) mechanism in Linux to monitor for suspicious activity and deploy targeted protections called “shields.” eBPF is a Linux technology that lets programs run in a controlled environment within the operating system’s kernel without modifying its source code or requiring a restart.

The tool’s capabilities include:

  • Live protection: Blocks vulnerable code paths without restarting systems, letting operators assess shield impact before enforcing them.
  • AI-assisted defense: Enables agents to investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields, and validate their effectiveness, with deployment remaining under human control.
  • Trusted deployment: Uses cryptographic signatures, Linux’s eBPF verifier, and kernel security controls to prevent unauthorized modifications.
  • Hardware-backed verification: Uses Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) to provide verifiable records of shields being loaded or removed.

Shirudo is designed for an agentic control plane with a configurable degree of autonomy when deploying mitigations. When a shield is deployed, the tool provides operators with hit counts, giving them insight into attempted exploits and where defenses need strengthening. Isovalent states that Shirudo is not limited to eBPF and can also modify application or userspace runtime bytecode to extend protection where needed.

⚙️ Key details

Shirudo is a rewrite of Tetragon, an open-source eBPF-based runtime security platform introduced by Isovalent in 2022. Tetragon also serves as the foundation for Cisco’s existing Live Protect technology. Isovalent, a cloud networking and security company acquired by Cisco in 2024, developed the tool.

Component Description
Test Case Researchers demonstrated that custom-generated shields could successfully block a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without interrupting its operation.
Distribution Shields will be distributed as cryptographically signed ‘.bee’ packages through an OCI registry.
Execution The tool can be activated through a command-line interface and doesn’t require a daemon to run permanently on the machine.
Compatibility The tool’s capabilities are limited to Linux because Mac and Windows have not implemented the components needed to be effective, according to Marcus Hutchins of Expel.

The two companies plan to provide “ready-to-use” mitigations in the form of tested shields, along with vulnerability disclosures, until patching is possible. While there is “genuinely so much runtime exploit mitigation potential with eBPF,” Marcus Hutchins noted that it may not be a good idea to let AI agents write rules that could impact the kernel.

🚀 Availability

Shirudo is open-source under BSD and GPL licenses. It comes with a quick-start guide as well as “getting started” documentation from Isovalent. On December 15, OpenAI will provide a technical rundown of how the tool works and how it combines eBPF and artificial intelligence to detect and counter new attacks in a deep-dive webinar.

The researchers state: “The Shirudo project is only the beginning, but it already shows the true potential of combining agents as a workforce with machine interfaces to let agents output what they are best at: code.”

#OpenAI #Cisco #LinuxSecurity #eBPF #Shirudo #RuntimeProtection

Source: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits

item.title: Recent cyber incidents not linked to AI
item.description:
Recent cyber incidents not linked to AI

Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA—it’s been a really bad week in cyberspace.

🔍 Overview

  • But, amazing as it might seem, these are not related.
  • As far as we know, they’re not the result of cyberattacks.
  • They’re not even related to AI.

⚙️ Infrastructure Challenges

  • Our computerized infrastructure is vulnerable and fragile.
  • Much of it is old, and has been incrementally patched and upgraded.
  • A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense.
  • And more and more of it is centralized: the same systems affecting many different aspects of our lives and society.
  • In many cases, it just barely works.
  • And when it fails, it tends to fail badly.

💡 Economic Drivers

  • There are a lot of technological reasons why this is true, but they are all downstream of the economic ones.
  • The technologies we rely on are built and maintained within our economic system—and that’s where the core problem lies.
  • Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, recoverability—these are all essential parts of reliable technology, but they are all costs.
  • More importantly, they are inefficient: costs that feel wasteful until something bad happens.
  • Modern shareholder capitalism, and private equity in particular, squeeze all inefficiencies out of a company in pursuit of near‑term profits.
  • Competition, with multiple companies competing to do the same thing, is another inefficiency.
  • Monopolization removes that in pursuit of near‑term profits.

🔧 Risks and Failures

  • The result is brittle systems, single points of failure.
  • They’re more susceptible to cyberattack—both human and AI‑fueled—and more susceptible to random mistakes.
  • The more we allow unregulated capitalism to privatize gains while socializing risks, the more we should expect these sorts of failures.

🔄 The Path Forward

  • Fixing this is technical, but it’s political first.
  • It requires changing incentives, and that involves regulation and control.

#Cybersecurity #AI #Infrastructure #Capitalism #Regulation

Source: We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For - Schneier on Security

item.title: Threat actors compromised 24 Check Point servers across 22 organizations in cyberespionage campaign
item.description:
Threat actors compromised 24 Check Point servers across 22 organizations in cyberespionage campaign

Threat actors exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign targeting 22 organizations, according to threat intelligence firm GreyNoise. The activity, tracked as GT13, was confirmed as ongoing between October 17 and November 2, though researchers believe the campaign remains active given the threat actors’ persistent access to Check Point devices. The 22 victim organizations are spread across 17 countries and include government entities, financial services providers, and companies in the energy, transportation, mining, and manufacturing sectors.

🔍 Overview

The attackers launched their operations from 99 IP addresses that appear to come from compromised Check Point devices and ExpressVPN exit nodes. GreyNoise detected the activity and noted it resembled cyberespionage operations, although the attacker’s motivation could not be conclusively determined. The researchers assessed that GT13 operated an AI-powered offensive tool, based on observed behavior, automation, and custom tooling, but this use of AI in the campaign remains unconfirmed.

🧩 How it works

The attack chain began with unknown means of initial compromise, though GreyNoise could not determine when or how the Check Point servers were breached. During post-compromise stages, the researchers observed the exploitation of CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass in Check Point SmartConsole that allows attackers to obtain an application login token and authenticate with administrator privileges. A Rejetto HTTP File Server, compromised by exploiting CVE-2026-61500, was used as an operational relay for managing intrusions and collecting stolen data from the compromised environments.

⚙️ Key details

The attackers leveraged automation and custom tooling, observed across more than 1,400 network sessions, 800 command-line artifacts, and 1,200 file-related activities. Their activities included:

  • Stealing firewall databases, credentials, configuration data, and internal certificate authority files
  • Generating a new certificate in one victim’s environment
  • Unloading security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections
  • Conducting internal network reconnaissance and attempting lateral movement

On October 26, the attacker performed a bulk certificate management operation across all 24 compromised Check Point servers, which failed, but still helped GreyNoise identify victims. The researchers also observed attempts to exploit multiple additional vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF), and CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script).

The campaign targeted additional enterprise systems including:

System Vulnerability Notes
Citrix NetScaler CVE-2023-4966 Targeted in lateral movement
Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2024-21893 Targeted during campaign
VMware vCenter CVE-2021-21972, CVE-2023-34048 Multiple vulnerabilities exploited
Microsoft Exchange CVE-2021-26855/34473 Targeted during intrusions
Microsoft Netlogon CVE-2020-1472 Part of lateral movement attempts

BleepingComputer has contacted Check Point to ask if they have better visibility into those attacks and which flaw was exploited for initial access, and we are waiting for their response.

💡 Why it matters

Although GreyNoise lost visibility into the campaign operations on November 2, the researchers believe it could still be ongoing. The company has notified international government partners and CERTs to alert impacted organizations and shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) that could help identify additional intrusions or block future attempts. Check Point warned about CVE-2026-16232 in July, marking it as an actively exploited zero-day vulnerability.

The campaign demonstrates sophisticated attack capabilities using compromised infrastructure and automation tools to conduct large-scale credential theft and lateral movement across critical infrastructure sectors including government, finance, and energy.

#cybersecurity #CheckPoint #GreyNoise #GT13 #cyberespionage #AI

Source: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations

item.title: Authorities Warn More Major Tech Outages Likely as AI-Driven Upgrades Create System Vulnerability
item.description:
Authorities Warn More Major Tech Outages Likely as AI-Driven Upgrades Create System Vulnerability

Recent weeks have seen a cascade of high-profile disruptions—including a nationwide FAA ground stop, a multi-day Outlook outage, and a JPMorgan Chase banking outage—prompting US intelligence and tech leaders to warn that more such events are inevitable.

📢 Official Warnings

Both Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Microsoft President Brad Smith have stated that the American public should expect continued disruptions.

  • Jay Clayton (CNN): “We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages.”
  • Brad Smith (CBS): “I think we have to be prepared, frankly, for the coming months because this isn’t the type of thing that just gets done in a couple of weeks … The whole information infrastructure of the world is in effect being upgraded right now.”

🔧 Why Outages Are Increasing

Microsoft President Brad Smith explained that AI is accelerating the discovery of system vulnerabilities.

“AI has made it easier to find flaws, and then you can either use that knowledge to patch the code, or if you’re a bad actor, you can use that knowledge to try to hack into systems.”

Recent attacks have targeted government and commercial systems, including the USDA, JP Morgan, and major supermarkets.

🛡️ What Authorities Recommend

Clayton emphasized that the public should be prepared for significant investment in two areas:

  • Upgrading aging infrastructure
  • Expanding cybersecurity measures

🚨 Outlook for the Coming Months

Authorities agree that any major technological shift—especially one involving widespread changes in computing and applications—will inevitably bring instability. Whether caused by AI-assisted cyberattacks or human error during system patching, more outages appear inevitable as the global information infrastructure undergoes rapid modernization.

#cybersecurity #systemoutage #AIrisk #infrastructure

Source: We haven’t seen the last of the major tech outages

item.title: CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of Critical Cisco Expressway Vulnerability
item.description:
CISA Warns of Active Exploitation of Critical Cisco Expressway Vulnerability

The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has warned federal agencies that attackers are actively exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway devices. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76466, enables unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected devices. Russian cybersecurity company F6 reported that attackers used an unnamed AI assistant to exploit this vulnerability, gaining root access on internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices and moving laterally across internal network clusters. CISA added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and mandated federal agencies to patch within three days under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, while urging all network defenders to prioritize remediation.

#cisa #cisco #vulnerability #cybersecurity #ai-security

Source: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks

item.title: CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists
item.description:
CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists

CrowdSec is an open-source, participative security solution that offers crowdsourced server detection and protection against malicious IPs. It operates as an all-in-one IDS/IPS and WAF for Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes environments, allowing users to detect bad behaviors and actively remediate threats through a shared community blocklist.

🔍 Overview

  • CrowdSec is an open-source security solution that is participative by design.
  • It provides IDS/IPS (Intrusion Detection/Prevention System) and WAF (Web Application Firewall) capabilities.
  • It supports Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • It features a crowdsourced blocklist of malicious IPs.
  • Detection rules are available under the MIT license.

🧩 How it works

  • Log Analysis: The Security Engine detects bad behaviors by analyzing log sources and HTTP requests.
  • Decoupled Architecture: Following a “Detect Here, Remedy There” approach, users can parse logs on one machine and block threats at a firewall, reverse proxy, or CDN on another.
  • WAF Capabilities: The AppSec component is built on Coraza, allowing SecLang rules and the OWASP Core Rule Set to load as-is. It also supports a YAML rule format.
  • Bot Mitigation: AppSec can answer suspicious requests with a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge at tunable difficulty, stopping headless browsers and scrapers while allowing verified crawlers like Googlebot to pass.
  • Community Blocklist: An IP identified as malicious by one user is added to a curated list, proactively blocking that IP for all other users before it reaches their systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • Scenarios: Ships by default with scenarios for brute force, port scan, and web scan.
  • Customization: Users can extend protection by picking more scenarios from the Hub or creating their own.
  • Remediation: Allows active remediation using Remediation Components.
  • Comparison: Unlike fail2ban, CrowdSec decouples detection and remediation; unlike ModSecurity or naxsi, it shares IP reputation and remediation layers with the log-based engine.

🚀 Availability

  • Installation is available for Linux, Windows, Docker, OpnSense, and Kubernetes.
  • The Community Blocklist is available in real-time.
  • Detection rules are hosted on the CrowdSec Hub.

#CrowdSec #Cybersecurity #IDS #WAF #OpenSource #BotDetection

Source: crowdsecurity/crowdsec

item.title: Microsoft Prints Issue with November 2026 Hotpatch and Forcepoint DLP
item.description:
Microsoft Prints Issue with November 2026 Hotpatch and Forcepoint DLP

Microsoft has identified a compatibility issue affecting printing functionality for certain users after installing the November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch. The problem specifically impacts systems running Windows 11 24H2 or later, where the KB5132043 update conflicts with the Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent solution.

🔍 Overview

The conflict causes the Print Spooler service to fail starting, leading to printing disruptions. Affected users may encounter a greyed-out print option or errors when attempting to select a printer.

🧩 How it Works

The incompatibility arises between:

  • The November 2026 Windows 11 hotpatch (KB5132043)
  • The Forcepoint DLP Endpoint Agent endpoint data loss prevention solution

⚙️ Key Details

Component Status
Affected Systems Windows 11 24H2 and later
Originating Update KB5132043 (November 2026 hotpatch)
Impact Print Spooler service fails to start
Symptoms Print option greyed out, printer selection errors

🚀 Availability

While no permanent fix is currently available, Forcepoint has provided a temporary workaround document accessible through the Forcepoint support portal for signed-in customers.

💡 Why It Matters

This issue extends beyond just printing problems. Microsoft also reported that the same KB5132043 hotpatch is causing installation and launch issues with Office and third-party applications on Windows 11 systems. These known issues differ from standard November 2026 Patch Tuesday security updates, which affect different scenarios—specifically printing complex documents on Windows Server 2016 or later and Windows 10 or later client devices.

Windows Autopatch, Microsoft’s cloud-based enterprise service announced in April 2022 and available starting July 2022 for customers with Windows 10/11 Enterprise E3 license or greater, delivers these hotpatch updates. The service was configured to apply these updates by default for eligible devices managed through Microsoft Intune and Graph API on systems with May 2026 Windows security updates installed.

#Windows #Microsoft #SecurityUpdate #Forcepoint #Hotfix

Source: Microsoft confirms Windows printing issues affecting Forcepoint users

item.title: Peruvian Call Center Operator Sentenced for $15 Million Fraud Scheme
item.description:
Peruvian Call Center Operator Sentenced for $15 Million Fraud Scheme

A Peruvian call‑center operator, Carla Magaly Alcedo Mendoza, was sentenced to eight years in prison for running a multi‑year fraud scheme that stole $15 million from more than 30,000 Spanish‑speaking U.S. residents.

🔍 Overview

  • Alcedo managed Peruvian call centers linked to fraud and extortion from Jan 2013 to Dec 2018.
  • The operation targeted Spanish‑speaking Americans, first offering free services or products, then impersonating U.S. government officials and lawyers to demand payment.
  • Victims were threatened with court action, arrest, and immigration consequences in unsolicited phone calls.

🗓️ Timeline

  • March 2023: Alcedo arrested in Peru.
  • April 2025: Extradited to the United States.
  • Pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud after an 18‑count indictment.
  • Received an eight‑year prison sentence.

💰 Impact

  • Defrauded over 30,000 Spanish‑speaking U.S. residents of $15 million.
  • “The scheme spanned several years and thousands of victims made payments to Alcedo. Collectively, the scheme was responsible for defrauding more than 30,000 Spanish‑speaking residents of the United States out of $15 million,” the Department of Justice said.
  • “These criminals preyed on hardworking Americans, using fear and intimidation to steal millions of dollars. They deliberately targeted Spanish‑speaking communities, impersonating government officials and threatening innocent people with arrest and legal consequences,” added Acting US Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas.

⚖️ Legal outcome

  • Alcedo was the tenth defendant extradited from Peru and sentenced in this scheme.
  • Ten other Peruvian call‑center owner‑operators and four distribution‑center owner‑operators have been convicted so far.

📊 Broader context

  • June 2026 FTC warning: Americans lost $3.5 billion to impersonation scams in 2025, with losses nearly tripling since 2020 and $920 million stolen by government impersonators.
  • April 2025 FBI Internet Crime Report: U.S. victims lost nearly $21 billion to cyber‑enabled crimes in 2025.

#Fraud #Extradition #CallCenter #Cybercrime

Source: Call center operator gets 8 years for helping scam 30,000 Americans

item.title: SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository
item.description:
SafeLine Emerges as Top GitHub Trending WAF Repository

SafeLine has newly appeared as a top-ranked GitHub trending repository for Go projects, establishing itself as a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) designed to protect web applications from attacks and exploits.

🔍 Overview

SafeLine is a self-hosted Web Application Firewall (WAF) to protect web apps from attacks and exploits. A web application firewall helps protect web apps by filtering and monitoring HTTP traffic between a web application and the Internet.

🧩 How it Works

Unlike a proxy server that protects a client machine’s identity, a WAF operates as a reverse-proxy, shielding the server by routing client requests through the firewall before reaching the server. A WAF protects web apps by filtering, monitoring, and blocking malicious HTTP/S traffic while preventing unauthorized data from leaving the application. This is achieved through policies that distinguish between malicious and safe traffic.

⚙️ Key Details

SafeLine’s core capabilities include:

Capability Description
Block Web Attacks Defends against SQL injection, XSS, code injection, os command injection, CRLF injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal, and other web attacks
Rate Limiting Thwarts DoS attacks, bruteforce attempts, traffic surges, and abuse by throttling excessive traffic
Anti-Bot Challenge Blocks bots and crawlers while allowing human users through challenge mechanisms
Authentication Challenge Requires password entry for visitors when enabled, blocking unauthenticated access
Dynamic Protection Dynamically encrypts HTML and JavaScript code with each visit to the web server

Additional features include defenses for web attacks, proactive bot abuse defense, HTML & JS code encryption, IP-based rate limiting, and Web Access Control List.

🚀 Availability

SafeLine has achieved significant recognition on GitHub:

  • #1 GitHub Trending Repository
  • #1 Go Repository of the Day
  • #1 Go Repository of the Week
  • #9 Go Repository of the Month

💡 Why It Matters

The rise of SafeLine highlights growing community interest in self-hosted, open-source security solutions for web application protection, offering organizations an auditable alternative to commercial WAF offerings.

#WAF #cybersecurity #GoLang #GitHub #WebSecurity

Source: chaitin/SafeLine

item.title: Shared Responsibility for AI Agents Remains Undefined Across Major Vendors
item.description:
Shared Responsibility for AI Agents Remains Undefined Across Major Vendors

Five organizations have published guidance on responsibility for AI agents, but no consensus has emerged on who is ultimately responsible for agent behavior. While traditional cloud security has clear separation of duties between vendors and customers, AI agents act as non-deterministic intermediaries, making the separation of responsibilities less clean. The available guidance approaches the issue from different angles, ranging from specific task assignments to descriptions of broader security layers. To address this, organizations need to determine who owns each agent, what permissions it holds, and how it operates across systems.

🧩 How it works

In cloud security, models like the AWS Shared Responsibility Model establish a clear division: vendors handle infrastructure security, while customers are responsible for the data and the actions taken. For example, if data is copied from AWS to SFDC, each vendor secures their infrastructure, but the customer owns the action.

AI agents complicate this framework. They send authenticated, authorized requests that can be compromised or rogue. A rogue agent has either misunderstood its instructions or acted inappropriately—a type of error that is not necessarily a mistake in the human sense. Because agents act as intermediaries between the user and the request, and they are not deterministic by nature, the line between vendor and customer responsibility becomes blurred.

⚙️ Key details

Five specific organizations have published guidance on this topic:

  • Microsoft: Published an AI agent shared responsibility model featuring a matrix for IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS deployments.
  • CSA and CoSAI: Published shared responsibility models.
  • AWS: Provided security guidance for AgentCore, applying its general shared responsibility model without a specific agent-specific model.
  • Anthropic: Published guidance titled “Trustworthy agents in practice.”

Only two of these organizations assign ownership of an agent’s identity, and they split that ownership differently. No publication agrees on who is responsible for the agent’s behavior. Approaches vary: some assign specific tasks to providers and customers, while others describe security layers or broader stakeholder roles.

💡 Why it matters

Frontier AI labs are clear about their immediate responsibilities: making models more robust, better guarded, and harder to hijack. They are equally clear about their limitations: they cannot understand the specific business context of an action. For instance, an agent deleting files from Google Drive could be acting maliciously or performing a normal task; the system cannot distinguish between the two. Consequently, builders bear final responsibility for the behavior and permissions of the systems they assemble. While tools like Claude Code include checks such as automated classifiers to block actions driven by hostile content, and vendors like OpenAI, Cursor, and GitHub offer approval prompts and sandboxes, these capabilities do not automatically resolve the question of accountability. As new protocols like MCP are introduced, they may conceptually denote expanded responsibility for those who built them, but the lack of unified ownership remains a critical gap for organizations deploying agents.

#AIAgents #CloudSecurity #Microsoft #AWS #Anthropic #SharedResponsibility

Source: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap

item.title: Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data
item.description:
Cleverbridge Breach Exposes Customer Payment Card Data

Cleverbridge, an e-commerce platform that provides services to software and SaaS companies, disclosed that a security breach resulted in the theft of customers’ payment card information. The stolen data includes credit card numbers and CVV security codes.

🧩 Company Background

Cleverbridge enables software and SaaS companies to sell products, process payments, and manage subscriptions. The platform lists numerous technology brands among its customers, including:

  • Red Hat
  • SUSE
  • Tenable
  • Veeam
  • Jamf
  • Sony
  • Parallels

🔍 Incident Timeline

According to a security incident disclosure, the company detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026. Systems were temporarily taken offline to contain the breach and were brought back online the same day. The investigation subsequently determined that a third party copied payment card data stored on the platform.

Affected customers began receiving notifications on November 20, 2026.

⚙️ Data Stolen

A breach notification shared with BleepingComputer reveals that the stolen information includes:

  • Payment card numbers
  • Expiration dates
  • CVV/CVC security codes

The notification explicitly states that no other personal data, such as names, contact details, or billing information, were copied. The notice specifies that the affected card ends in a placeholder sequence.

🚫 What Was Not Involved

Cleverbridge confirmed that the incident was not a ransomware attack. Attackers did not encrypt any of the company’s systems. The company has not disclosed how the attackers gained access, how long they remained in the systems, or the total number of affected customers.

💡 Response and Remediation

Cleverbridge has notified data protection authorities, law enforcement, payment card networks, and payment partners regarding the incident. The company is working with TransUnion’s Cyberscout to distribute breach notifications and provide affected customers with complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance. Customers are advised to review their payment card statements for any unauthorized transactions.

#DataBreach #Cleverbridge #PaymentSecurity #Cybersecurity #CreditCardTheft

Source: Cleverbridge warns hackers stole credit card numbers, CVVs in data breach

item.title: Microsoft Suffers Data Breach Following Entra Connect Health Vulnerability
item.description:
Microsoft Suffers Data Breach Following Entra Connect Health Vulnerability

Microsoft is warning organizations that it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to gain unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information.

🔍 Overview

  • Microsoft Entra Connect Health is a cloud-based monitoring service that allows administrators to monitor the health, performance, and alerts of their on-premises identity infrastructure through the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  • Microsoft discovered the vulnerability in the Entra Connect Health API on November 9, 2026, after it was first introduced on July 23.
  • An investigation determined that the flaw was exploited, allowing unauthorized parties to access tenant and service-monitoring metadata and potentially modify Connect Health monitoring configurations.
  • Microsoft concluded its investigation on November 20, 2026, determining that unauthorized read-only access to tenant-level metadata occurred, with no unauthorized configuration changes identified.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Email addresses belonging to tenant technical contacts and administrator accounts were exposed.
  • Tenant IDs, display names, initial domain names, country codes, and regional information were exposed.
  • Microsoft Entra license tiers and directory synchronization status, including whether synchronization was enabled and the last synchronization timestamp, were exposed.
  • Connect Health onboarding status was exposed.
  • An expired certificate previously used to register Connect Health agents with a Microsoft internal service that was decommissioned in late 2024 was exposed.
  • User passwords, password hashes, authentication tokens, valid cryptographic keys, on-premises server and Active Directory topology details, and Azure subscription information were not exposed.

🛠️ Timeline and Remediation

  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19, 2026, to prevent further exploitation.
  • Microsoft finished its investigation on November 20 and began notifying affected organizations.
  • No software updates or other customer remediation are required to address the vulnerability.
  • Microsoft published a PowerShell script at https://aka.ms/ConnectHealth/scripts allowing administrators to view the types of tenant metadata that could have been exposed.

💡 Recommendations

  • Alert security teams to potential targeted phishing and social-engineering attacks targeting exposed administrator email addresses and tenant information.
  • Ensure privileged accounts use phishing-resistant multifactor authentication.
  • Review Connect Health configurations.
  • Examine Microsoft Entra audit and sign-in logs for suspicious activity.

#Microsoft #EntraConnectHealth #DataBreach #Cybersecurity

Source: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data

item.title: Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens
item.description:
Rackspace Spot Breach Exposes Kubernetes Secrets and API Tokens

Rackspace has warned customers that hackers breached its Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials. The intrusion allowed unauthorized parties to deploy workloads and access sensitive Kubernetes secrets within customer clusters.

🔍 Overview

Rackspace disclosed the breach in a notification to affected customers, stating that attackers accessed parts of the platform on November 17, 2026, between approximately 00:20 and 22:00 UTC. The company learned of the intrusion on November 18 after receiving a customer report and confirmed that the recipient’s organization was affected that same day.

⚙️ Key details

  • Access Method: An unauthorized party used leaked credentials to act as legitimate users in some customer organizations.
  • Actions Taken: Attackers created pods in Kubernetes clusters, read Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and volumes.
  • Exposure Risk: Attackers could have read any Secret stored in an affected user’s clusters, as well as any Spot API tokens or refresh tokens held by that user.
  • Indicators: The breach was associated with IP address 23.224.79.106, IP range 23.224.0.0/15, and suspicious Kubernetes pod and object prefixes including i1, glm-, and probe.

🛡️ Remediation and Response

Rackspace stated that it has revoked affected tokens and sessions, removed the unauthorized pods, rotated keys, and strengthened access controls and monitoring. Affected customers were instructed to:

  • Reissue their Spot API tokens.
  • Replace refresh tokens used in automation tools.
  • Download fresh Kubernetes configuration files.
  • Rotate credentials stored in their cluster Secrets.
  • Analyze logs associated with databases, container registries, Git repositories, cloud storage, and third-party services dating back to November 17 to identify possible abuse of exposed credentials.

The breach caused an extended outage of the Rackspace Spot administration console, temporarily preventing customers from managing their clusters or rotating credentials. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and Chief Growth Officer of Platform9, explained that the team deliberately disabled access while securing its infrastructure. Rackspace announced that service was fully restored on November 21.

#Rackspace #Kubernetes #CloudSecurity #DataBreach

Source: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets

item.title: Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android
item.description:
Signal Adds Protections Blocking AI Assistant Screen Access on iOS and Android

Signal has announced new protections that block screenshots on iOS 27 and prevent AI assistants from capturing conversations on supported Android devices. These measures are designed to stop built-in AI assistants, such as Siri and Gemini, from accessing private conversation content while performing tasks for users.

🔍 Overview

The announcement follows Signal’s introduction of a feature in May 2025 that blocked Microsoft’s Recall screenshot-capturing feature on Windows 11. Signal’s president, Meredith Whittaker, stated that the company is now taking similar measures to restrict agentic systems built into iOS 17 and on Android versions where an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal screen can be detected.

Signal engineers spent months investigating how AI systems access app data. They designed targeted protections to block all extraction pathways, which were verified through reverse engineering. The protections specifically target OS-level features like Siri’s Onscreen Awareness and Google’s Gemini Intelligence, which can otherwise capture chat content as it appears on the screen.

⚙️ Key Details

The new protections operate differently across platforms:

  • iOS: The protection blocks screenshots entirely. This includes preventing users from taking screenshots of Signal conversations for legitimate purposes. On the iOS app, users can verify that “Block Siri AI” is enabled by navigating to Settings > App Security.
  • Android: Signal automatically enables Screen Security when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen.
  • macOS: Signal is currently unable to provide screenshot-blocking protection for macOS. For macOS 27 users, Signal recommends adding the app to the Excluded Apps list under System Settings > Siri to prevent proactive access to message content.

Signal notes that the protections are automatically activated when possible, though specific app version numbers were not provided.

💡 Why it Matters

Signal warns that AI agents embedded deep in operating systems pose an “existential threat” because they can access conversation data through methods beyond simple screen reading. Whittaker notes that these vulnerabilities leave apps with limited options for protecting users and expose sensitive private data belonging to all conversation participants.

In response, Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide detailed documentation disclosing all potential access mechanisms. The company urges these operating system vendors to give developers a clear way to opt out of AI access across screens, files, notifications, and APIs.

#Signal #Privacy #AIAgents #Security #iOS #Android

Source: Signal to block Siri, Gemini AI from capturing chats on iOS, Android

item.title: x64dbg-MCP Server enables AI control of debuggers via Zig
item.description:
x64dbg-MCP Server enables AI control of debuggers via Zig

The x64dbg-MCP Server, a native MCP (Model Context Protocol) plugin for x64dbg, has been released, allowing MCP-compatible AI assistants to control the debugger programmatically over HTTP. Built with the Zig programming language, the solution is designed to be dependency-free, requiring only a single binary drop-in deployment without the need for .NET, Python, or other runtimes.

🧩 How it works

The server exposes the full functionality of x64dbg through standard protocols, enabling AI agents to perform complex debugging tasks. It supports both Streamable HTTP and SSE (Server-Sent Events) transports using JSON-RPC 2.0, ensuring compatibility with both new and legacy MCP clients.

  • Transport Protocols: Uses Streamable HTTP + SSE for dual-transport compatibility.
  • Authentication: Implements mandatory Bearer token authentication; the token is auto-generated on the first run and required for every request to prevent unauthorized access.
  • Execution: The plugin is a pure native application with zero dependencies, cross-compiling to both x32 and x64 architectures from a single codebase.

⚙️ Key details

The MCP server provides extensive control over the debugging environment, covering a wide range of operations from code analysis to memory management.

  • MCP Tools: The evidence cites 84 MCP tools for full debugger control, including disassembly, stepping, breakpoints, memory allocation, registers, modules, threads, call stack, pattern scanning, string extraction, xrefs, symbols, bookmarks, PE analysis, OEP detection, module dumping, PEB/SEH inspection, and tracing. (Note: One quote also references 72 MCP tools covering the workflow).
  • Event Callbacks: Includes 22 event callbacks covering init, stop, breakpoint, exception, step, attach/detach, DLL load/unload, and thread events.
  • Configuration: Users can change IP, port, and token settings via a dialog in the Plugins menu, which auto-restarts the server upon saving.
  • Auto-Start: The MCP server initiates automatically when x64dbg launches.
Component Details
Default Port (x64) 0.0.0.0:9094
Default Port (x32) 0.0.0.0:9095
Language Zig
Dependencies None (No .NET, Python, or runtimes)
Architectures x32 and x64

🚀 Availability

Deployment is designed to be straightforward, allowing users to build and deploy the plugin across different operating systems.

  1. Copy the contents of the dist/ directory into the x64dbg root folder to deploy both x32 and x64 versions.
  2. Launch x64dbg; the MCP server starts automatically.
  3. For connections from WSL or remote machines, set the bind address to 0.0.0.0 in the config dialog and use the host’s IP address.

The tool supports cross-compiling Windows plugins from Linux, macOS, or WSL environments from a single command.

#x64dbg #MCP #Zig #AIAssistants #Debugging

Source: duty1g/x64dbg-mcp-server

item.title: AI Formal Verification Tools Combat Code Slop and Security Risks
item.description:
AI Formal Verification Tools Combat Code Slop and Security Risks

The term “slop” has become the industry’s word of the year for 2026, describing low-quality output from large language models. As AI-generated code increases, software engineers are turning to formal verification systems—tools that use mathematical proofs and logic to ensure correctness—to mitigate this daily concern.

🧩 How it works

Formal verification relies on “solvers” for satisfiability modulo theories (SMT). The most prominent is cvc5, an automated reasoning engine co-created by Stanford Corbel Professor (Research) of Computer Science Clark Barrett.

  • cvc5 is widely used in companies like Amazon, including in specification analysis and test generation for Kiro, Amazon’s agentic development environment.
  • A new entrant, &Truth (pronounced ‘and truth’), builds on Lean, an open-source programming language and proof assistant. &Truth combines AI with automated reasoning to construct proofs that Lean checks, aiming to create a “verification machine” that reads code in any language to prove it satisfies stated requirements.
  • Axiom Math develops AxiomProver, an AI system that generates Lean proofs, alongside AXLE, a toolkit for manipulating those proofs. Axiom uses formal verification to provide correctness feedback for training its mathematical reasoning systems.
  • Harmonic’s automated theorem prover, Aristotle, uses Lean heavily, ensuring that AI writes proofs while Lean checks every step, so results never rest on the AI being right.

⚙️ Key details

  • Theorem focuses on cybersecurity, stating that “Verification is the only defense that holds while adversaries scale.” It has collaborated with Anthropic on formal software verification at scale.
  • &Truth prioritizes cybersecurity, including scanning C code to ensure memory safety.
  • Lean is increasingly used by frontier models to solve difficult math problems. For instance, GPT-6.2 Astra produced what is believed to be the first Lean proof of Smoktunowicz’s Gap Theorem, and Anthropic used Lean to formalize Fermat’s Last Theorem in a 13-million-line project.
  • Anthropic reported that Opus 5.5 achieved a 50% solve rate on 36 small verification tasks using about 40% fewer tokens than Opus 5, with a collaboration with Theorem describing “LLM-scaled formal verification” as a promising approach for security guarantees.

#FormalVerification #AI #Lean #Cybersecurity #cvc5

Source: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification — Latent Space

item.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence details AI agent hack on universities
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence details AI agent hack on universities

Amazon Threat Intelligence shared findings from an investigation into a Chinese-nexus threat actor who used autonomous AI agents to conduct hacking operations with minimal human involvement. The investigation revealed a campaign targeting IP addresses associated with universities in East Asia outside mainland China over a 48-hour period beginning September 8, 2026.

🔍 Overview

On September 10, 2026, Amazon Threat Intelligence identified a server with a publicly hosted instance of Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework, running without authentication. Because the operator left the server publicly accessible, the operational history of the platform was visible to anyone on the internet. This visibility included project configurations, actor prompts, and AI output. The operator wrote prompts in Simplified Chinese, and the timestamps in executed scripts were configured to China Standard Time.

🧩 How it works

Cairn is built as a research and problem-solving engine for defenders. Operating it is simple: given a starting point and an objective in plain language, it coordinates multiple AI agents to find a path to that goal. The actor in this campaign gave the agents a simple goal: “obtain shell access.” Based on a list of targeted IP addresses and that goal, the AI agents planned, executed, and adjusted their approach as they learned, without the operator choosing each next step.

⚙️ Key details

The campaign included several operations that varied widely in complexity and outcome. During the campaign, the agents found a zero-day in an open-source application and used it to gain full control of a server.

Operation Target Duration Key Actions
Redis instance at one university ~16 hours 148 sequential actions; abused replication feature, escaped scripting sandbox, wrote to config files, corrupted memory, attempted Log4Shell injection
University GPU server > 6 hours Researched public presence to build list of ~80 usernames; tested > 30,000 credential combinations against SSH, admin dashboard, network storage, VPN, and campus portal
Open-source medical imaging AI application Not specified Identified framework, mapped API endpoints, found upload endpoint with a filename parameter

In the Redis operation, when initial attempts to take control failed, the agents mapped the internal Docker network topology through a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in a co-located Qdrant instance and launched credential sprays against PostgreSQL, SSH, and several other services. None of these attempts succeeded. In the GPU server operation, the agents never found a working login. Against the medical imaging application, the agents successfully identified the framework and mapped its API endpoints.

💡 Why it matters

These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening. Defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable, as the agents kept adapting for nearly a full day without human direction, even when specific operations did not succeed.

#Cybersecurity #AIAgents #ThreatIntelligence #Amazon #Zero-day #AutonomousHacking

Source: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own | Amazon Web Services

item.title: BADBOX 3.0 Botnet Returns with Record Ad Fraud Activity
item.description:
BADBOX 3.0 Botnet Returns with Record Ad Fraud Activity

The BADBOX malware botnet has resurfaced, generating a record 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day through infected Android-based devices.

🔍 Overview

  • The BADBOX 3.0 variant has grown into the largest documented ad-fraud operation by daily bid request volume.
  • It was first discovered in early 2023 on a T95 Android TV box bought on Amazon.
  • Germany’s cybersecurity agencies warned in December 2024 that the botnet had infected tens of thousands of devices.
  • In March 2025, a large-scale disruption operation took place where HUMAN and Shadowserver cut off more than 500,000 BADBOX 2.0 devices from their control servers, while Google removed 24 apps that spread the malware from Google Play.
  • Google later sued the botnet’s operators, saying the BADBOX 2.0 had infected over 10 million Android-based devices by April 2025.

🧩 How it works

  • The malware performs ad fraud by playing video ads in hidden windows while impersonating legitimate streaming apps to make the requests appear legitimate.
  • HUMAN also observed fraudulent server-side ad insertion (SSAI) requests that tricked advertisers into believing ads were played on streaming devices, even though no actual device or video ad was involved.
  • A proxying module also enrolled infected devices in one of 11 residential proxy networks without the owners’ knowledge or consent.
  • One of those networks, PXYEDGE, was identified as the rebranded successor to IpMoYu, a residential proxy service previously linked to BADBOX 2.0.
  • The researchers say PXYEDGE advertised approximately 200,000 proxy nodes, while their monitoring showed unique connections peaking at around 340,000.
  • HUMAN says some of the ad fraud traffic was also routed through these residential proxies to appear legitimate and evade anti-abuse filters.

⚙️ Key details

  • The infected devices fetch malware modules from public code repositories, while the same payloads are also mirrored across various hosting platforms for redundancy and to resist takedowns.
  • HUMAN says it also participated in Google’s disruption of the related XCPE malware operation earlier this month, which included taking down multiple C2 domains used by BADBOX 3.0.
  • Additionally, one of the malware repositories was taken down, while HUMAN says its systems now filter fraudulent advertising traffic associated with BADBOX 3.0.

💡 Why it matters

  • Users should only buy certified Android devices from reputable manufacturers and ensure that Play Protect is available and active.

#BADBOX #Malware #AdFraud #Android #Cybersecurity

Source: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking 40 billion daily ad requests

item.title: Chinese-linked actors misuse AI pentesting tool Cairn to exploit MONAI Label zero-day
item.description:
Chinese-linked actors misuse AI pentesting tool Cairn to exploit MONAI Label zero-day

In early September 2026, a Chinese‑nexus threat actor used the autonomous AI‑agent platform Cairn to discover and exploit a path‑traversal zero‑day in the open‑source medical‑imaging application MONAI Label, gaining root control of targeted servers.

🔍 Overview

  • Campaign observed between September 8‑10 2026.
  • Attributed with moderate confidence to a Chinese‑nexus threat actor.
  • Primary targets were East Asian educational institutions outside China.
  • Attack leveraged the autonomous AI‑agent platform “Cairn”.

🧩 How it works

  • Operators instructed Cairn agents to “obtain shell access”.
  • Agents autonomously discovered a path‑traversal zero‑day in MONAI Label.
  • Within 11 minutes they mapped the API, wrote a Python reverse shell to sitecustomize.py, and triggered an endpoint to gain root.
  • After the initial compromise, operators supplied a proxy to a second university network running the same vulnerable software for further targeting.

⚙️ Key details

  • Cairn is a legitimate pentesting tool designed to coordinate multiple AI agents for research and defense.
  • The attackers left their Cairn instance publicly accessible without authentication, exposing the operation.
  • A 16‑hour, 148‑action attempt to take over a Redis server failed.
  • A separate six‑hour attempt on a university GPU server tried >30 000 credential combos and also failed.
  • Amazon Threat Intelligence shared two IP addresses used in the campaign: 142.4.98.145 and 142.4.107.34.
  • MONAI Label maintainers issued a security update on November 18 2026 after being notified.

📈 Impact

  • Successful compromise gave complete root control of a medical‑imaging server.
  • Similar Cairn abuse was documented in a large‑scale credit‑card stealing operation (Gambit Security) and in an attack on a U.S. aerospace organization (Google).
  • Amazon warned that AI agents can find and exploit vulnerabilities faster than manual security investigations.

🛡️ Mitigation

  • Apply the November 18 2026 MONAI Label security update.
  • Monitor for publicly exposed Cairn instances.
  • Adopt automated defensive measures to keep pace with AI‑driven attacks.

#Cairn #AIAgents #ZeroDay #Cybersecurity

Source: Hackers use autonomous AI tool Cairn to find zero-day, take over server

item.title: FBI Investigates Second Reported System Breach in Two Months
item.description:
FBI Investigates Second Reported System Breach in Two Months

FBI systems have reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, this time targeting the agency’s National Crime Information Center (NCIC). The NCIC is used to share information between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies.

🔍 Overview

  • The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the NCIC system, according to CNN’s reporting citing two people briefed on the investigation.
  • The intrusion was reportedly discovered in recent days.
  • It is unclear when the breach occurred, how the attackers gained access, or whether any information was stolen.
  • The FBI has not publicly confirmed the incident and did not respond to CNN’s request for comment.
  • BleepingComputer contacted the FBI on Friday evening with questions about the reported breach but has not received a response.
  • This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

⚙️ Key details

  • The National Crime Information Center is an FBI-operated database used across the United States to share information about wanted and missing persons, outstanding arrest warrants, stolen vehicles and firearms, protection orders, and other criminal justice records.
  • Police officers routinely use the system during traffic stops, criminal investigations, and background checks.
  • It remains unclear whether attackers accessed sensitive law enforcement records stored in NCIC or whether the intrusion affected system availability.

🧩 Context and Prior Incidents

  • The reported breach comes two months after the ShinyHunters extortion group claimed to have breached FBI systems by exploiting an unpatched Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability.
  • The earlier attack targeted a third-party platform associated with the FBI’s recruitment website, FBIJobs.gov, with ShinyHunters claiming to have stolen sensitive information.
  • The FBI subsequently launched an investigation leading to the arrests of suspected ShinyHunters members, including a Canadian cybersecurity executive reportedly linked to the attacks.
  • There is currently no indication that the latest NCIC incident is connected to ShinyHunters or the earlier breach.

#FBI #Cybersecurity #DataBreach #NCIC #LawEnforcement

Source: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database

item.title: Introducing Agentbox, a Sandboxing Tool for Running AI Agents in Docker
item.description:
Introducing Agentbox, a Sandboxing Tool for Running AI Agents in Docker

A new project called agentbox has been introduced to help developers run AI agents inside secure sandboxes. This project is currently in early-stage development, meaning users may experience breaking changes between releases.

🔍 Overview

The tool is designed to work with any Docker-compatible runtime. To run it, you need a VM and Docker installed. While setting this up can be done in a variety of ways, the provided instructions are for Colima. To install it, download the agentbox binary from GitHub Releases; the installer defaults to the ~/.local/bin directory.

🧩 How it works

When initializing, the tool simplifies the process of configuring and running agents:

  • Interactive Setup: It prompts interactively for the project name, agent, mode, and IDE when needed. It then generates the docker compose and network policy files for the sandbox.
  • Secrets Directory: It automatically creates the host secret directory at ~/.config/agent-sandbox/secrets (with mode 0700) if it is missing. On version 0.17.0 and earlier, you must create this directory yourself before starting the sandbox.
  • Read-Only Proxy: The proxy mounts the secrets directory as read-only, even if you do not have any secrets yet.
  • Configuration Auditing: To inspect your configuration after initialization, you can run agentbox policy config to output the effective network policy, or agentbox compose config for the combined docker compose stack.
  • Yolo Mode: Because you are running the agent inside a dedicated sandbox, you can even try yolo mode!

⚙️ Key details

Depending on the agent image you are using, you should follow its specific setup instructions. Additionally, developers should be aware of several extension and IDE limitations within the sandbox environment:

Tool or Plugin Compatibility Status
Copilot’s IntelliJ plugin Cannot complete auth in a devcontainer
Google Gemini No official plugin available for JetBrains
OpenCode No JetBrains extension available
Pi No IDE extensions available
Hermes No IDE extensions available

#AIAgents #Sandboxing #Docker #DeveloperTools #Security

Source: mattolson/agent-sandbox

item.title: OpenAI Updates Safeguards to Combat Adversarial Distillation in GPT-6.2 Models
item.description:
OpenAI Updates Safeguards to Combat Adversarial Distillation in GPT-6.2 Models

OpenAI has introduced updated protections to detect and disrupt adversarial distillation, a process where actors use a frontier model’s outputs to train a separate model with similar capabilities but fewer safeguards. These strengthened defenses, specifically implemented in GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, are designed to prevent the unauthorized extraction of protected reasoning traces that could be used to facilitate cyberattacks or other harmful activities.

🔍 Overview

Distillation is a machine-learning technique where a student model learns from data produced by a teacher model. Adversarial distillation poses significant safety risks because it allows a second model to acquire advanced capabilities without inheriting the original model’s safety protocols. This could lead to a model providing assistance with cyberattacks or biological research that the original model would have refused or blocked.

🧩 How it works

OpenAI focuses on protecting the “chain-of-thought”—the internal intermediate steps a model generates while working toward an answer. These reasoning traces are more valuable training data than final answers because they contain information that the final response may omit.

  • Teacher-Student Dynamic: The original model (teacher) produces training data used to train the second model (student).
  • Capability Transfer: Internal studies show that student models trained on exact reasoning traces generally outperform those trained only on reasoning summaries.
  • Offensive vs. Defensive: A model that helps defenders find software vulnerabilities could be distilled into a student model that helps an attacker exploit those same vulnerabilities.

⚙️ Key details

OpenAI has deployed a safeguard stack that operates at two complementary levels to prevent extraction attempts.

Level Protective Measures
Request Level Model behavior, classifier checks, and API-level protections
Campaign Level Monitoring request and account-level signals for coordinated extraction patterns

Internal adaptive evaluations using automated red-teaming demonstrated the effectiveness of these updated safeguards in preventing the recovery of protected reasoning.

Model Safeguard Version Attack Success Rate
GPT-6 Astra Original Safeguards 54.0%
GPT-6.2 Astra Updated Safeguards 0.2%

💡 Why it matters

Protecting reasoning traces serves as a defense against the transfer of dangerous capabilities, even when the underlying task itself is permitted under standard usage policies. By limiting the availability of these traces, OpenAI aims to prevent the creation of models that could assist with offensive cybersecurity or the development of harmful pathogens. These updates align OpenAI’s protections more closely with the safeguards used for biology and cybersecurity domains.

#AISafety #Cybersecurity #GPT6 #MachineLearning

Source: Combatting adversarial distillation

item.title: Ransomware Recovery Firm Founder Charged With Wire Fraud
item.description:
Ransomware Recovery Firm Founder Charged With Wire Fraud
