Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, co-founder of the Florida-based ransomware recovery firm RansomwareHelp, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation revealed that the company routinely paid ransomware attackers for decryption keys while claiming to victims that it used proprietary cryptographic tools.

🔍 The Allegations

The indictment, returned in Rhode Island, alleges that the 52-year-old Miami-based co-founder routinely paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and charged victims a significant markup for work that was never actually performed. RansomwareHelp, a six-year-old Florida business, had claimed on its website that it used “advanced cryptographic tools” to restore 100 percent of data, servers, and systems. The company explicitly stated it did not promote, intermediate, or pay ransom to threat actors on behalf of its clients.

⚙️ FBI Sting Operation

The FBI set up a sting operation in which investigators posed as both a ransomware victim company and a fictitious ransomware group. Investigators, acting as victims, supplied the company with a phony ransomware note and expressed a desire not to pay a ransom. RansomwareHelp initially reiterated its policy against negotiating with or making ransom payments.

However, Palacio soon contacted the fake ransomware group run by the FBI and requested the lowest possible price for a decryptor. FBI investigators responded with a price of 0.2 bitcoin, or around $13,000. Less than 48 hours later, Palacio allegedly informed the fake victim company that the diagnostic assessment was successful and quoted a decryption cost of $13,260. The following day, the indictment states, Palacio messaged the fictitious group to reduce the ransom demand to $4,000 for the purchase of a decryption tool. The agreed-upon price was around $6,000 in bitcoin, yet Palacio charged the FBI’s fake victim firm $16,010, including a $2,750 diagnostic fee and the $13,260 full fee.

💡 Real-World Impact

In 2024, Paul Ihme, co-founder of the security firm Soteria, heard from a small accounting firm that had paid RansomwareHelp a diagnostic fee to recover from a Lockbit ransomware infection. RansomwareHelp sent a proposal for a recovery price of $438,880, claiming this included “professional configuration of forensic servers” and “expert engineering hours of programming to configure decryption algorithms.”

The proposal claimed the recovery process involved reverse engineering the ransomware encryption using “510 preconfigured forensic servers of the maximum quantitative capacity located in different parts of the world.” Ihme believes RansomwareHelp insisted on unrestricted remote access into the victim’s network using Anydesk remote desktop software in part to delete copies of the ransomware notes left by the attackers. A review of the network found only one copy of the ransom note, unearthed from a backup snapshot. When the security firm connected to the Lockbit chat server using the provided user ID, they discovered RansomwareHelp had already been negotiating with the Lockbit extortionists for several days, pleading not to reveal their involvement to the victim.

#Ransomware #FBI #WireFraud #Cybersecurity #LawEnforcement

Source: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud

item.title: Unit 42 tracks Com-affiliated vishing and data extortion campaigns
item.description:
Unit 42 tracks Com-affiliated vishing and data extortion campaigns

Unit 42 has tracked and responded to numerous waves of vishing attacks conducted by Com-affiliated threat actors in recent months, leading to data theft and extortion attempts. Since early 2026, the team has attributed multiple data theft and extortion attempts to Bling Libra and other Com-affiliated threat actors.

🔍 Overview

  • The attacks have targeted data-rich industries, such as financial services, healthcare, and legal services.
  • Targeted organizations were primarily located in the U.S., UK, and Australia.
  • Attackers use the threat group and activity cluster naming conventions tracked by Unit 42.

🧩 How it works

  • Initial Access: Attackers establish access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization.
  • MFA Bypass: These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time.
  • Persistence: In multiple instances, attackers have enrolled an unauthorized MFA device within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence.
  • Exfiltration: Attackers have automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to target Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint content.
  • Extortion: Following exfiltration, attackers have sent Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees, claiming data theft and directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site.

⚙️ Key details

  • CL-CRI-1264: Identified in September 2026, this activity cluster primarily targets healthcare, pharmaceutical, and other medical organizations. Attackers targeted employees on both corporate workstations and personal mobile devices, reusing a single device named “Pixel 10a” across compromised accounts.
  • CL-CRI-1274: Also identified in September 2026, this cluster avoided re-prompting for Duo MFA by replaying a persistent “keep me signed in” session token. They then used scripted access through python-requests and the Microsoft Graph SDK to collect and exfiltrate data from SharePoint and OneDrive environments. Extortion messages were sent internally via email and Microsoft Teams.
  • CL-CRI-1192: During an investigation attributed to this cluster (which Google tracks under UNC6671), a malicious browser extension named “Google Chrome” (manifest version 1.6.111) was identified. The extension was not on the Chrome Web Store and was downloaded from an attacker-controlled server at oskeysetup[.]com, requiring manual sideloading using Developer Mode.

💡 Why it matters

  • Organizations can access tailored adversary intelligence, direct analyst consultations, and specialized exposure tracking through Unit 42 Threat Intel Services and its Deep and Dark Web Service.
  • If an organization thinks it might have been compromised or has an urgent matter, it should contact the Unit 42 Incident Response team.

#Unit42 #ThreatIntel #Vishing #Com-affiliated #Cybersecurity

Source: Dialing for Data: Inside the Com’s High-Profile Heists

item.title: Updates on Production-Grade Microservice Boilerplates and Wazuh Security Platform
item.description:
Updates on Production-Grade Microservice Boilerplates and Wazuh Security Platform

Recent developments highlight updates regarding a production-grade microservice boilerplate and the features of the Wazuh open-source security platform.

🔍 Overview

A production-grade microservice boilerplate has been introduced, featuring tools such as GORM, Goose, Swag, Zerolog, Validator.v10, GitOps, Kubernetes, Kustomize, ArgoCD, and Istio. Additionally, Wazuh continues to serve as a free and open-source platform used for threat prevention, detection, and response across on-premises, virtualized, containerized, and cloud-based environments.

⚙️ Key details

  • The microservice boilerplate builds a production-ready containerized RESTful API server application using Go standard library net/http and the Chi router.
  • Development environments use golang:1.27-alpine (~1180 MB) and postgres:19-alpine (~440 MB), while production uses distroless/static-debian13:nonroot (~46 MB).
  • For high-traffic systems with large PostgreSQL tables, arranging fixed-width columns by decreasing alignment requirements can reduce tuple alignment padding and potentially minimize storage size, a technique called “Column Tetris”.
  • Wazuh’s architecture consists of an endpoint security agent and a management server.
  • Wazuh agents scan monitored systems for malware, rootkits, suspicious anomalies, hidden files, cloaked processes, and unregistered network listeners.
  • The Wazuh server uses a signature-based approach to intrusion detection with a regular expression engine.
  • Wazuh provides native integration with the Docker engine to monitor images, volumes, network settings, and running containers.
  • Cloud infrastructure monitoring includes integration modules for Amazon AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.

💡 Why it matters

These tools help organizations build robust containerized RESTful APIs with automated GitOps deployment via ArgoCD, while maintaining comprehensive security, threat detection, and regulatory compliance with standards such as PCI DSS, GPG13, and GDPR using Wazuh.

#Microservices #Go #Kubernetes #Security #Wazuh

Source: learning-cloud-native-go/myapp Source: dokku/dokku Source: wazuh/wazuh

item.title: Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors
item.description:
Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors

Amazon is upgrading the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness to use Strands harness, an open-source agent harness released under an Apache 2.0 license. This update introduces lifecycle hooks, automatic prompt caching, and proactive context management alongside new security features for enterprise-grade tool execution and data protection.

🔍 Overview

With this upgrade, the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness operates on top of Strands harness, which acts as an assembled agent foundation with recommended instructions, tools, and context management. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runs this foundation as a managed AWS service, eliminating the need to provision compute, bundle and host the agent loop, manage session scaling, or operate tool-execution infrastructure.

🧩 How it works

Each agent session runs in a secure, kernel-isolated microVM in the AgentCore runtime, which connects the harness to the production services required by enterprise agents:

  • Session Execution: Handled automatically with managed compute, scaling, and high availability.
  • Integration Services: Connects directly to session persistence, streaming responses, usage metadata, observability, AgentCore memory, Identity, and Gateway.
  • Control Balance: Developers retain control over instructions, tools, models, permissions, and lifecycle policies while AgentCore manages the underlying execution environment.

⚙️ Key details

The upgrade introduces a suite of native features designed to reduce latency, cost, and complexity:

  • Lifecycle Hooks: Allows developers to apply custom deterministic checks and notifications at defined points in the agent loop.
  • Prompt Caching: For supported Converse models, the harness caches system prompts, tool definitions, and conversation history to reduce latency and input token costs.
  • Context Optimization: Summarizes older conversation turns once the context window reaches a configurable threshold, running at about 34% lower token cost than other leading harnesses.

Built-In Tools

The upgrade brings several new built-in capabilities for managing agent workflows:

Tool Name Functionality
todo_write Maintains a structured task plan that can be restored in later sessions, even after context summarization.
subagent Delegates self-contained tasks to fresh worker agents and returns results to the parent.
web_fetch Retrieves content from specified webpages to provide up-to-date external context.
Filesystem Access Granular read, write, and edit tools to control the filesystem capabilities granted to agents.

💡 Why it matters

As agents interact with third-party tools, SaaS APIs, and web search engines, sensitive data (such as names, account numbers, or card details) can leave the AWS account and compliance scope through tool arguments. To address this, AgentCore Gateway fronts every tool an agent uses and supports request and response interceptors via AWS Lambda.

By adding Skyflow Detect to AgentCore Gateway as an interceptor, sensitive entities are detected and replaced with reversible vault tokens before data reaches tools, and restored before the agent reads the tool’s results.

This configuration enables three protection modes:

  • Shield the tool: Strips sensitive values from arguments on the way out and restores them in results on the way back, protecting third-party APIs from receiving customer identities.
  • Shield the model: De-identifies prompts, history, files, and tool results before the model reads them.
  • Shield the document: Replaces original document links from tools with clean copies before the agent opens them.

For example, a large European bank uses these tools to investigate card disputes. When an agent searches the web for a merchant, the Skyflow interceptor replaces the customer’s name with a reversible token (e.g. [NAME_AJbrIud]). The search provider receives a safe query, while the authorized analyst still sees the correct customer details in the agent’s final response.

🚀 Availability

  • Strands Harness: Open-source under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • Skyflow Detect Interceptor: Open source on GitHub.
  • Skyflow Vault: Available on the AWS Marketplace.

#AmazonBedrock #AIagents #AWS #OpenSource #DataSecurity

Source: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks | Amazon Web Services Source: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway | Amazon Web Services

item.title: ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29
item.description:
ASUS patches critical Control Center Express vulnerabilities in v1.7.29

ASUS released Control Center Express v1.7.29 to address three critical vulnerabilities that could allow remote attackers to gain administrative control of the management console and the devices it manages.

🔍 Overview

  • Control Center Express is a central dashboard used by IT administrators to monitor and remotely manage fleets of PCs.
  • The product is marketed to businesses and IT service providers and supports more than 200 ASUS business, workstation, and Corporate Stable Model motherboards.

⚙️ Fixed Vulnerabilities

CVE Severity Type Impact
CVE-2026-114202 Critical (CVSS 10.0) Hard‑coded cryptographic key Unauthenticated remote attacker can forge an authentication token and gain administrator privileges with no prerequisites
CVE-2026-114204 Critical Hard‑coded key Remote attacker with low privileges can forge a session token for a recently logged‑in account
CVE-2026-114205 Critical Authorization flaw Low‑privileged user can create an administrator account

🚀 Availability

  • Versions earlier than v1.7.29 are affected. The security bulletin lists versions through v1.7.27; the status of v1.7.28 is unclear.
  • Affected users should install v1.7.29, then update agents on managed devices via Select Function → Client Agent Updater and verify the agent versions.

📦 Related Updates

  • Control Center Enterprise and Control Center Datacenter received patches for CVE-2026-126574, a critical authorization flaw that lets a low‑privileged Viewer role change an administrator’s password.
  • Armoury Crate was updated to fix CVE-2026-112115, a high‑severity privilege escalation flaw affecting all versions up to 6.7.2.

💡 Why it matters

  • The unauthenticated remote exploit (CVE‑2026‑114202) provides full administrative control without any user interaction, representing a worst‑case scenario for enterprise IT environments.
  • Even the lower‑privilege flaws could enable attackers to elevate their access, potentially compromising large fleets of managed PCs.
  • Prompt patching is essential to maintain the integrity of the management console and the devices under its control.

#ASUS #Security #Vulnerabilities #ITManagement

Source: ASUS warns of critical hard-coded key flaw in Control Center Express

item.title: Broadcom Patches VMware vCenter Zero-Day Exploited by Chinese Group
item.description:
Broadcom Patches VMware vCenter Zero-Day Exploited by Chinese Group

Broadcom has released emergency security updates to fix a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass vulnerability that Chinese-linked hackers have exploited in zero-day attacks since September 2026.

🧩 How it works

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, affects the VMware Directory Service in vCenter Server, a management platform used to manage VMware virtualized environments. According to Broadcom, the flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a vulnerable vCenter Server to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.

  • Successful exploitation allows attackers to obtain administrative access to vCenter, giving them control over the virtual machines managed by the server.
  • The vulnerability affects vCenter regardless of whether Enhanced Linked Mode is enabled.

Mandiant researchers documented that attackers exploit the flaw to create a remote authentication bypass, establishing an authenticated session as administrator@vsphere.local. Using this session, attackers can execute arbitrary commands and acquire files, including the data.mdb database, by leveraging the vCenter Server Directory Service (vmdird) RPC interface vmdirdbcp.

⚙️ Key details

  • Patch Availability: Broadcom patched the vulnerability on November 19 in VMSA-2026-0009. This update also fixes four other vulnerabilities affecting VMware SDDC Manager and VMware Tools for Windows.
  • Affected Software: The advisory notes that users are affected if running any version of VMware vCenter, SDDC Manager, or VMware Tools for Windows prior to the versions listed as “fixed” in the VMSA. This includes vCenter and SDDC Manager deployed standalone and as part of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSphere Foundation, VMware Telco Cloud Platform, and VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure, as well as VMware Tools installed in Windows virtual machines.
  • Workarounds: Broadcom states there are no official workarounds for the vulnerabilities, although network restrictions and firewall controls can help reduce exposure.
  • Urgency: The company considers the vCenter vulnerability an emergency update, urging organizations to install patches as soon as possible.
Tool/Malware Function
SLIMSAVAGE Web shells deployed to maintain persistent access and scan for VMware systems
BONESAW Custom Golang exploitation tool used to exploit CVE-2026-123890 and steal the directory database
SAWSNAKE Enables “Golden SAML” attacks to forge authentication tokens and bypass MFA
CAGEMATCH Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and transfer files
BEARBONES Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and steal credentials
LAZYBONES Web shell/backdoor used to execute commands and maintain access

🚨 Attack Context

Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group revealed that a suspected Chinese state-sponsored hacking group tracked as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) exploited CVE-2026-123890 in early September 2026. The VMware exploitation was part of the same intrusion campaign, where attackers first compromised BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances (exploiting zero-day CVE-2026-102764) before moving laterally into internal Linux systems.

After gaining access to an internal Linux appliance, the hackers deployed SLIMSAVAGE web shells, escalated privileges to root, and scanned the internal network. They then used BONESAW to compromise a VMware vCenter Server. BONESAW creates a vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO) administrator account and steals the server’s directory database. It can also extract SAML signing keys, allowing attackers to forge authentication tokens. Following exploitation, attackers deployed SAWSNAKE and additional backdoors to move deeper into virtualized environments, access ESXi hosts, and extract sensitive information, including Windows Active Directory database files.

💡 Why it matters

Mandiant says the use of two zero-day vulnerabilities in the same campaign, along with multiple malware families tailored to the targeted platforms, demonstrates the threat actor’s technical expertise. Researchers urge admins to apply the VMware security updates as soon as possible and configure additional security controls to protect their virtualization infrastructure.

#VMware #Broadcom #CVE-2026-123890 #ArmoryCastle #ZeroDay #InfoSec

Source: VMware patches vCenter zero-day exploited in attacks since September

item.title: Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released
item.description:
Critical PHP and Drupal Security Updates Released

On November 19, security updates were released for 18 vulnerabilities in the PHP development ecosystem, alongside the patching of a critical remote code execution flaw in the Drupal content management system. These updates address severe security issues that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable servers.

🚀 PHP Security Updates

The PHP dev team released updates for all supported branches, with versions 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, and 8.2.36 now available. Security firm Aikido reports that these updates address 18 CVEs affecting PHP’s core engine, session handling, PHP-FPM, CGI, and other components. The most serious flaw, CVE-2026-129289, is a critical PHP-FPM request smuggling vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.2. This vulnerability affects certain nginx, Apache, HAProxy, and LSAPI configurations that reuse backend connections to PHP-FPM; standard configurations that do not reuse connections are not affected. As a temporary mitigation, administrators can disable persistent backend connections to ensure they are closed after each request. Third-party maintainer Ondrej Surý has released patched packages for unsupported versions back to PHP 5.6, and Aikido has released hardened container images for similar unsupported versions.

🧩 PHP Vulnerability Details

The following vulnerabilities were fixed in the November updates:

CVE Identifier Description
CVE-2026-129474 Use-after-free vulnerability involving magic method backtraces
CVE-2026-129496 Timezone cache use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-126714 Vulnerability involving partially overwritten session files
CVE-2026-115560 Session serializer mismatch vulnerability
CVE-2026-129291 PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free vulnerability
CVE-2026-128090 PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass vulnerability

Additional fixes address memory corruption, information disclosure, cross-site scripting, denial-of-service issues, and unsafe handling of HTTPS and FTPS URLs. As a temporary mitigation for CVE-2026-115560, PHP recommended disabling session upload progress by setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0. This vulnerability was disclosed in an October 23 informational advisory.

🛡️ Drupal Critical Flaws

The Drupal Security Team has patched a critical remote code execution vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-132165. Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, this flaw allows anonymous users to exploit the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, potentially leading to site takeover or remote code execution. The security team warned that at least one critical vulnerability can be exploited by anonymous users. Drupal administrators are urged to upgrade to versions 10.6.22, 11.3.22, or 11.4.13. For those who cannot immediately upgrade, it is recommended to secure the Drupal installer by blocking access to /core/install.php in the web server configuration or the .htaccess file. This update also addresses a moderately critical gadget chain vulnerability (CVE-2026-132166). The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has flagged five Drupal vulnerabilities as exploited in the wild since November 2021.

#PHP #Drupal #SecurityUpdates #Vulnerabilities #CVE

Source: PHP security updates fix 18 flaws, including critical RCE bugs Source: Drupal patches critical RCE flaw, warns exploits may surface quickly

item.title: F5 Patches NGINX nginx2root Vulnerabilities Enabling Remote Code Execution
item.description:
F5 Patches NGINX nginx2root Vulnerabilities Enabling Remote Code Execution

F5 has released security updates for multiple NGINX vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws dubbed “nginx2root.” These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers and can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access to the underlying host.

Researchers at Xint, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, and Rapid7 discovered the two primary HTTP/2 vulnerabilities independently. Xint researchers demonstrated that by chaining one of these flaws with a separate vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s SCTP subsystem, an attacker can escape an NGINX Docker container and gain root privileges.

🧩 How it works

The “nginx2root” vulnerabilities involve memory corruption and session management errors within the NGINX worker process:

  • CVE-2026-123007: A flow-control bug that causes memory corruption in an NGINX worker. It impacts versions 1.31.8 down to 1.9.5.
  • CVE-2026-123633: A use-after-free issue that occurs when NGINX accepts HTTP/2 connections and proxies them to a backend. When the worker runs low on connection slots, it may close an active connection and free memory that a request is still using.

⚙️ Key details

Vulnerability Description
CVE-2026-123007 Memory corruption flaw in NGINX worker via HTTP/2 flow-control.
CVE-2026-123633 Use-after-free vulnerability affecting HTTP/2 requests proxied to backends.
CVE-2026-118899 High-severity DoS flaw causing an infinite loop over TLS 1.3.
CVE-2026-121810 Use-after-free vulnerability affecting HTTP/3 reverse proxying.
CVE-2026-123634 Use-after-free vulnerability affecting DNS resolution with subrequests.
CVE-2026-113425 Use-after-free vulnerability affecting mail proxy authentication.

🚀 Availability

F5 has fixed these issues in the latest versions of NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus. System administrators are recommended to upgrade immediately:

  • NGINX Open Source: Update to 1.30.7 (stable) or 1.31.9 (mainline).
  • NGINX Plus: Update to 37.0.8.1 or 37.3.0.1.

As a temporary mitigation for the two “nginx2root” flaws, administrators can disable HTTP/2, although this does not address the other vulnerabilities included in the security update.

💡 Why it matters

Exploitability depends heavily on specific server configurations. Security researcher Florian Roth notes that these flaws are exploitable in non-default configurations and may not be an imminent threat for most deployments. The vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on a reachable listener, and CVE-2026-123633 specifically requires NGINX to be proxying requests to a backend.

According to Censys, approximately 8.8 million NGINX services were potentially exposed to CVE-2026-123007 as of November 19, based on version numbers and HTTP/2 support. More than 511,000 previously exposed services have already been patched or mitigated.

#Cybersecurity #NGINX #InfoSec #Linux #CloudSecurity

Source: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers

item.title: F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities
item.description:
F5 Warns Customers to Patch Critical BIG-IP Vulnerabilities

US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.

🔍 Overview

  • Status: NEW
  • Five stack-based buffer overflow flaws affect the BIG-IP Access Policy Manager (APM) and BIG-IP iRules programmable scripting feature.
  • Unauthenticated threat actors can exploit these issues to terminate the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) and execute arbitrary code remotely on vulnerable configurations.
  • F5 also released engineering hotfixes for a high-severity BIG-IP APM SAML vulnerability (CVE-2026-126822) caused by an integer underflow weakness.

🧩 How it works

  • Tracked vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-121805, CVE-2026-120292, CVE-2026-120285, CVE-2026-116953, and CVE-2026-123637.
  • Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts during exploitation.
  • This is a data plane issue only with no control plane exposure.

🚀 Availability

  • F5 stated there are no mitigation measures for these flaws and advised security teams to install the out-of-band hotfixes released on Wednesday.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 177,000 BIG-IP instances and over 14,600 IP addresses with BIG-IP APM fingerprints exposed online.

💡 Why it matters

  • Although F5 has not flagged any of these issues as exploited in attacks, admins should upgrade systems quickly.
  • Cybercrime and nation-state threat groups have often abused F5 vulnerabilities in the wild to breach corporate networks, map internal servers, hijack devices, deploy data-wiping malware, and steal sensitive files.

#Cybersecurity #F5 #Vulnerabilities #Patch

Source: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws

item.title: JPMorgan Chase Warns of Data Breach via Third-Party Cyberattack
item.description:
JPMorgan Chase Warns of Data Breach via Third-Party Cyberattack

J.P. Morgan Chase announced that it suffered a data breach following a cyberattack on a third-party service provider, which exposed customers’ personal information and marketing data. The bank stated that its services were not disrupted and the incident is unrelated to a service disruption that occurred earlier in the week.

🏦 Banking Sector Impact

J.P. Morgan Chase Bank is the largest U.S. bank by assets, with about $4.1 trillion as of June 2026, and its consumer banking division reports about 78 million active digital customers. The bank’s announcement on X stated, “We have learned that third parties who provide services to the firm were the target of a cyber attack.” The bank further disclosed, “Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses.”

💳 Payment Networks Affected

Visa and Mastercard confirmed that they were involved in third-party incidents, though both have not confirmed any impact on customers or their core payment networks.

  • Visa: A spokesperson told BleepingComputer that the incident is “associated with an incident involving a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific.” Visa stated, “Visa’s systems were not involved and were not impacted. No payments data such as card numbers were affected.”
  • Mastercard: The company confirmed it was “informed of an incident at a third-party provider that resulted in the exposure of limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information – from a small subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program.” A spokesperson assured that “There is no impact to the Mastercard payment network or the ability for people to use their cards.”

🏭 Third-Party Provider

On November 11, 2026, the n0n ransomware group claimed responsibility for an attack on Qubole, a cloud data analytics company owned by Idera, suspected to be the third-party provider used by the financial institutions. Qubole is used for cloud data analytics, automated processing, real-time analysis, and reporting.

📊 Stolen Data and Extortion

Between October 14 and 26, 2026, the n0n ransomware group allegedly used compromised Qubole credentials to access customers’ AWS environments through IAM roles configured to grant Qubole access. The group claimed to have stolen 53.9 GB across 30,743 files directly from Qubole, including customer contracts, pricing records, staff and trial-user information, and production data. Additionally, they claimed to hold nearly one petabyte of data from Qubole’s customer networks. The n0n group leaked the claimed data on its extortion site on November 16, 2026, stating that their extortion demands were ignored after contacting Qubole and the affected companies.

#JPMorganChase #Ransomware #Cybersecurity #Qubole #DataBreach #VisaMastercard

Source: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info

item.title: N-able cyberattack disrupts Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services
item.description:
N-able cyberattack disrupts Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services

N-able reported a cyberattack that breached a server in its Hosted Cloud environment, leading to a worldwide outage of the Mail Assume and SpamExperts services.

🔍 Overview

  • Attackers breached one of N-able’s servers, causing a major outage of Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services worldwide.
  • The outage initially was attributed to a “combination of platform configuration and service dependencies.”
  • N-able later confirmed unauthorized access to a server in the Hosted Cloud environment.

📅 Timeline

  • On Tuesday, N-able described the disruption as a configuration and dependency issue affecting the Americas, Asia‑Pacific, and Europe.
  • The following day, UI and API access were disabled and unauthorized server access was confirmed.
  • An email alert was sent to customers after the attack was detected.

⚙️ Impact

  • Email flow and spam filtering continued to operate; N-able said there is no evidence that attackers accessed customer data or mailboxes.
  • Customers could not sign in to the control panel, view or release quarantined messages, review logs, or modify domain configurations until services are restored.
  • The management portal (dashboard) and supporting services for quarantine, logging, and mailbox synchronization were taken down.

🛡️ Response

  • N-able disabled UI and API access, took down the management portal, and began mitigation steps.
  • The company is hardening services to reduce the risk of recurrence.
  • Investigation is ongoing, with no current evidence of compromised customer data.
  • N-able clarified that the incident is unrelated to a separate N‑central outage caused by more than 30 zero‑day flaws.

💡 Why it matters

  • Highlights the risk of unauthorized server access even when core email delivery remains functional.
  • Demonstrates the importance of rapid customer communication and service isolation during a security incident.
  • Shows that a single breached server can impact globally distributed cloud email security services.

#N-able #Cyberattack #EmailSecurity #CloudOutage

Source: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage

item.title: NVIDIA Investigates Third-Party Partner Incident Following Gentlemen Ransomware Claims
item.description:
NVIDIA Investigates Third-Party Partner Incident Following Gentlemen Ransomware Claims

NVIDIA is investigating claims of a security breach after the Gentlemen ransomware group added the company to its dark web data leak site, though no proof of the breach has been shared yet.

🔍 Overview

  • The Gentlemen ransomware group listed NVIDIA on its dark web data leak site and threatened to release data with a countdown ending in nine days on November 28.
  • NVIDIA stated it has not found evidence that its systems were compromised, but is looking into a separate incident that may have affected a third-party partner.
  • An NVIDIA spokesperson told BleepingComputer: “We have found no indication that NVIDIA systems or networks were affected. We continue to monitor the situation.”

⚙️ Key details

  • The Gentlemen surfaced last year as a closed ransomware group before switching to a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) model.
  • The group offers affiliates up to a 90% cut of ransom proceeds.
  • It operates as a double-extortion group that exfiltrates sensitive data before encrypting systems and threatening to leak the information.
  • Since emerging, The Gentlemen has claimed more than 1,100 victims across manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, energy, education, and financial services sectors.

#NVIDIA #Ransomware #Cybersecurity #DataBreach

Source: NVIDIA investigating Gentlemen ransomware breach claims

item.title: Ransomware Defense: Detecting Pre-Encryption Attack Stages
item.description:
Ransomware Defense: Detecting Pre-Encryption Attack Stages

Ransomware attacks rarely begin with the ransomware payload itself. Operators first need an initial foothold, and common entry paths include exploitation of vulnerable internet-facing systems, abuse of stolen credentials, and social engineering. By the time encryption occurs, the intrusion may already include credential theft, privilege escalation, defense evasion, recovery sabotage, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. In data-extortion attacks, encryption may never happen at all, as operators steal data and threaten to leak it without encrypting anything.

🚀 Initial Entry Paths

Attacker entry into environments typically occurs through three primary vectors:

  • Vulnerable Systems: Unpatched, externally accessible services provide a route into the environment.
  • Stolen Credentials: Compromised credentials allow attackers to enter through legitimate remote-access or cloud services.
  • Social Engineering: This path targets users and the processes surrounding identity and access.

Once attackers establish access, they use stolen credentials and legitimate administration tools to move through victim environments before deploying ransomware.

🔍 Pre-Encryption Detection Signals

Defenders need to detect behaviors that precede encryption, not only the encryptor itself. Five high-value signals deserve immediate attention when monitoring for suspicious post-compromise behavior:

Signal Description
Defense tampering Attempts to stop security services, modify protection agents, load vulnerable drivers, or clear event logs.
Privilege escalation and lateral movement Unexpected privileged accounts, remote-execution tools spreading across hosts, or unusual server-to-server remote access.
Data exfiltration Unusual outbound transfers from systems that do not normally upload large volumes of data.
Recovery sabotage Deletion of shadow copies, backup catalogs, or recovery options using tools such as vssadmin.exe, wbadmin.exe, or bcdedit.exe.
Pre-encryption file behavior Rapid file enumeration, repeated read-write-rename activity, and encryption-like changes across local or network locations.

⚙️ Layered Defense Strategy

Stopping ransomware is rarely about a single control. A comprehensive strategy requires reducing opportunities for initial compromise, detecting and containing malicious activity when they do occur, and having a reliable way to recover if systems or data are affected.

  • Prevention: Reducing unnecessary internet exposure, prioritizing patching of high-risk systems, strengthening identity and access controls, and protecting email and collaboration channels.
  • Detection and Response: Monitoring endpoints for suspicious post-compromise behavior provides a layer when preventive controls do not stop the initial intrusion. Endpoint protection, email security, and extended detection and response (XDR) tools can identify and contain malicious activity across endpoints, email, and the wider environment.
  • Recovery: Integrated backup and recovery provide the path to restoring affected systems and data. It is important to note that this layer does not undo data theft, a critical distinction in double-extortion attacks.

#Ransomware #Cybersecurity #ThreatDetection #DataExfiltration

Source: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft

item.title: SBC Medical Group Exposes Data of 1.6 Million Individuals
item.description:
SBC Medical Group Exposes Data of 1.6 Million Individuals

SBC Medical Group disclosed in a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing that two separate cybersecurity incidents resulted in the unauthorized exposure of sensitive customer and employee information, affecting a total of 1.6 million people.

⚠️ The Breach

The company, a clinic management firm primarily operating in Japan with a limited U.S. presence and Nasdaq listing (SBC), revealed that the incidents impacted its Japan-based businesses. The breach was identified on November 16, 2026, when unauthorized access occurred to certain databases within a website system managed by the company’s Japanese subsidiary.

The data affected by this database incident included:

  • Basic personal information belonging to 1,624,000 people.
  • 255,416 reservation requests.
  • 217,769 inquiries submitted to SBC websites.
  • Thousands of treatment description records, image filenames, and customer reviews.
  • Approximately 20,000 employee account records containing names, IDs, and passwords.
  • Bank account and tax information for a subset of 459 employees.

🏥 The Tribeau Compromise

Simultaneously on November 16, SBC was notified of a second incident involving unauthorized access to clinic administrator accounts on Tribeau, a third-party booking platform. This breach affected reservation information for 12,641 people and accessed treatment names, dates, and fees for 6,804 patients who received treatment at 56 clinics using the service.

📊 Current Status

SBC confirmed that the attackers extracted customer information but stated that they have not confirmed unauthorized access to electronic medical records or information from the mySBC reservation site. The method of intrusion and full scope remain under investigation. As of the November 18 filing, the company had not seen evidence of misuse of the exposed data and could not estimate the financial impact of the incidents.

#SBCMedical #DataBreach #Cybersecurity #SECFiling #HealthcareSecurity

Source: Hackers steal data of 1.6 million SBC Medical Group customers

item.title: Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications
item.description:
Shannon: Open-Source AI Pentester for Web Applications

Shannon, an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs developed by Keygraph, has been released as an open-source agent that can be run locally from the command line.

🔍 Overview

  • Shannon is an autonomous AI pentester for web applications and APIs.
  • It analyzes source code to identify attack vectors and executes real exploits to prove vulnerabilities before they reach production.
  • It is developed by Keygraph.

🧩 How it works

  • Shannon analyzes the web application’s source code to identify potential attack vectors.
  • It then uses browser automation and command-line tools to execute real exploits against the running application and its APIs.
  • Only vulnerabilities with a working proof-of-concept are included in the final report. The policy is “No exploit, no report.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Shannon is open-source and runs locally from the command line.
  • The same Shannon agent also powers Keygraph’s commercial editions: Pro and Enterprise.

🚀 Availability

  • The repository is Shannon: the full open-source agent, run locally from your command line.

💡 Why it matters

  • By requiring a working exploit before reporting, Shannon ensures that only proven vulnerabilities are documented, reducing false positives and providing actionable results.

#AI #pentesting #cybersecurity #opensource #websecurity #AIagents

Source: KeygraphHQ/shannon

item.title: Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages
item.description:
Signal blocks screenshots on mobile to stop AI agents reading messages

Signal is restricting the ability to take screenshots on Android and iOS devices to prevent AI agents from reading users’ messages and other data.

🧩 How it works

Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen. The company is addressing privacy concerns by blocking the ability to take screenshots in the app on iOS 27 and Android, which should prevent Siri, Gemini, and other Android AI assistants from reading on-screen content. Users can restore screenshot capabilities in Signal’s app settings, but the president warns that doing so will “potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Limitations: The screenshot-blocking remedy is “incomplete” as it does not address alternative ways that AI agents can access app data, such as retrieving it via the device file system.
  • Platform Availability: Signal is currently unable to implement these protections on macOS.
  • Previous Precedent: Signal took a similar approach last year to prevent Microsoft’s controversial Recall feature from capturing secured chats.
  • Developer Tools: The service is struggling to develop a better solution due to the lack of available information regarding how AI agents are actually accessing application data.
  • Ecosystem Call: Signal is calling on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide “simple technical tools and accurate documentation” to app developers. More tools are also needed to prevent third-party agents, like Meta’s Muse, from using deep accessibility settings in apps like a “skeleton key” to access application data.

💡 Why it matters

Signal president Meredith Whittaker stated that the agentic AI capabilities built into operating systems that analyze on-screen information to learn more about the user are “undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” She urged OS providers to make it easier for app developers to control what data agents can access. Whittaker emphasized: “We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy.”

Whittaker noted that even where they are able to detect and block AI data access, major tech companies do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. She concluded: “We all need to recognize that the current integration of AI agents into the operating system, without these common-sense remedies, represents an existential threat to privacy at the application layer, and the ability of independent developers like Signal to protect your sensitive data,” adding that “Signal is the canary in the coal mine, but this affects the entire ecosystem and should galvanize anyone who cares about these fundamental rights.”

#Signal #AIAgents #Privacy #iOS27 #Android

Source: Signal is blocking Gemini and Siri AI from reading your screen

item.title: TfL data breach impacts 265,000 Oyster photocard customers
item.description:
TfL data breach impacts 265,000 Oyster photocard customers

Transport for London (TfL) announced that approximately 265,000 Oyster photocard customers may have had their account details exposed in a security incident discovered on November 16, 2026. The breach was identified after customers reported receiving emails from TfL’s mail systems requesting them to create an account.

🔍 Overview

TfL operates London’s public transport network, including the Underground, Overground, buses, trams, and the Elizabeth line, recording 3.53 billion passenger journeys in 2025/26. The Oyster photocard website has been taken offline, and data breach notifications are being sent to impacted individuals. The incident has been contained, and TfL has notified the UK’s Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO).

⚙️ Key Details

The data leak involved the following personal information:

  • Full names
  • Phone numbers
  • Email addresses
  • Home addresses
  • Dates of birth
  • Security questions and answers

TfL’s assessment indicates that passwords, bank and payment card details, journey information, and the names and dates of birth of children with Zip Oyster cards were not compromised. No evidence of misuse has been found so far.

💡 Why It Matters

The exposure of security questions and answers is particularly concerning because these details may be used for account access restoration. Customers who received the suspicious email should ignore it and remain vigilant for further activity. Once the Oyster photocard portal is restored, all photocard customers will be prompted to change their password, security question, and answer.

Recommendation Detail
Account Security Change passwords, security questions, and answers on Oyster photocard
Cross-Site Security Rotate security questions used at other sites
General Hygiene Change passwords on other services where the same information was used
Reporting Report suspicious activity to TfL Customer Services immediately

Oyster photocards remain valid for travel. Customers who need to renew their cards or check journey history can contact TfL’s Customer Services.

#DataBreach #TransportForLondon #OysterPhotocard #CyberSecurity #UK

Source: Transport for London breach exposes 265,000 Oyster card users’ data

item.title: 2026 U.S. Election Websites See Traffic Surge, Minimal DDoS Activity
item.description:
2026 U.S. Election Websites See Traffic Surge, Minimal DDoS Activity

Visitors to U.S. government election websites surged 363% on November 3, 2026, the day of the midterm elections, while Cloudflare recorded no major DDoS attacks on protected sites.

🔍 Overview

  • Traffic to state and local election websites reached about 602 million requests on Election Day, up from 130 million on November 1.
  • Overall traffic across Cloudflare’s global network rose only 12% during the same period.
  • Attacks focused on gaining access to internal systems and data rather than taking sites offline.
  • Major DDoS activity was absent on Election Day; only one significant DDoS occurred on November 2 targeting a California House candidate with 520,000 requests.

⚙️ Key details

  • Website vulnerability attempts were 180 times more frequent than DDoS attacks and ten times the rate seen across Cloudflare’s broader customer base.
  • Vulnerability exploit attempts rose from 200,000 per day in January to 2 million per day in October.
  • In the 12 months before the election, Cloudflare mitigated 392 million website vulnerability attacks on government election websites.
  • Cross‑site scripting attacks inject malicious code into web pages to capture administrator credentials or deface site content.
  • SQL injection manipulates database queries to potentially extract voter records or alter data.
    Attack Type Description
    Cross‑site scripting Injects malicious code into web pages to capture admin credentials or deface content
    SQL injection Manipulates database queries to potentially extract voter records or alter data

🚀 Availability

  • No escalation in attack volume and zero major DDoS incidents were detected across the 1,400 protected election-related websites on Election Day.
  • The only significant DDoS attack occurred on November 2, targeting a California U.S. House candidate and totaling 520,000 requests.
  • Traffic to state and local election websites was higher on Election Day than any other day in 2026, reaching approximately 602 million requests.
  • By contrast, traffic across the rest of Cloudflare’s network increased only 12% over the same period.

💡 Why it matters

  • Cloudflare’s free election protection programs (Athenian Project, Cloudflare for Campaigns, Project Galileo) helped protect more than 1,400 election‑related websites belonging to governments, candidates, parties, advocates, journalists and civil‑society groups.
  • Cloudflare launched its first election protection program in 2016 after widespread reports of cyberattacks targeting the U.S. elections.
  • Despite the surge in traffic and increased vulnerability attempts, cyberattacks did not disrupt the 2026 election, underscoring the effectiveness of the protective measures.

#Election #Cybersecurity #Cloudflare #DDoS #Vulnerability

Source: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections

item.title: AI‑Powered Autonomous Penetration Testing Platform REDCELL Launches
item.description:
AI‑Powered Autonomous Penetration Testing Platform REDCELL Launches

A new AI red‑team platform called REDCELL lets autonomous LLM agents run a full penetration test inside a Kali container and generate a polished report.

🔍 Overview

  • REDCELL orchestrates a team of LLM agents to plan, act, and report on security engagements.
  • The platform is built with FastAPI for the backend and React for the frontend, delivering a live operator console.
  • Legal use is limited to education, research, and authorized security testing; users must have explicit permission to test target systems.

🧩 How it works

  • An orchestrator (implemented with a LangGraph plan/act loop) receives high‑level objectives from a chat interface.
  • It delegates tasks to executor agents that run real tools inside a Kali Docker container via docker exec.
  • Agents can:
    • Execute shell tools (nmap, nuclei, Metasploit, etc.) and parse their output directly into findings.
    • Drive a real Chromium browser for JavaScript‑heavy apps, with the operator able to intervene.
    • Open listeners, capture reverse shells, and provide interactive terminals.
  • All activity (agent graph, findings, loot, terminals, browser stream) updates live over WebSockets or short‑polling.
  • The session’s model (chosen via LiteLLM) generates a PDF, JSON, and SARIF report, cleaned up to read like a human‑written document.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model flexibility – LiteLLM lets you plug in OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, local Ollama, or any supported provider.
  • Checkpointing – Each run saves progress; crashes or restarts resume where they left off.
  • Live steering – Operators type commands in chat to steer the orchestrator, reopen finished runs, or ask questions about the engagement.
  • Export options – PDF with executive summary, methodology, findings, and remediation; plus JSON and SARIF formats.
  • Notifications – In‑app toasts and browser notifications keep users aware of agent prompts or caught shells.

Dedicated tools

Tool Purpose
nmap Network scanning and host discovery
nuclei Vulnerability scanning
Directory & vhost discovery Enumerate web directories and virtual hosts
Metasploit search & run Exploit search and execution
run_command Execute any command without a dedicated tool

🚀 Availability

  • Session settings allow selection of execution server, model, and optional egress proxy, with built‑in connection tests.
  • Sessions can target a public Git repository or local folder for source‑code security reviews, mapping findings to file and line numbers.

💡 Why it matters

  • REDCELL provides a repeatable, automated workflow for penetration testing, reducing manual effort while keeping the operator in the loop.
  • By integrating live browser control and reverse‑shell handling, it reaches assets that traditional tools cannot.
  • The platform’s provider‑agnostic model stack and checkpointing make it adaptable to varied environments and compliance needs.

Use REDCELL only on systems you own or have explicit written permission to test, and stay within the legal scope of your jurisdiction.

#AI #PenTest #LLM #Automation #Cybersecurity

Source: martian56/redcell

item.title: Introducing the External Sandbox Pattern for Secure AI Agent Code Execution
item.description:
Introducing the External Sandbox Pattern for Secure AI Agent Code Execution

On November 17, 2026, a new project developed in collaboration with Prime Radiant introduced the external sandbox pattern. Under this pattern, code executed by an AI agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox, while the agent itself resides outside of that sandbox.

🔍 Overview

The external sandbox pattern separates the AI agent from the environment where its executed code runs. To demonstrate this pattern, three sandbox server implementations have been released. These sandboxes can be configured to receive API calls from AI agents such as Pi, Claude Code, or Codex whenever they need to execute code.

⚙️ Key features

  • Unified API: Each implementation offers the same localhost API.
  • Allow-list Proxy: An optional HTTP/HTTPS proxy to control exactly which hosts the agent’s code is allowed to communicate with.
  • Credential Replacement: A mechanism that allows the agent’s code to make authenticated API calls without sharing secret credentials directly with the agent.

🧩 Sandbox implementations

Implementation Description
external-sandbox-v86 A Node.js server that uses v86 to run Alpine Linux inside WebAssembly.
external-sandbox-container A Python web server that runs the sandbox in Alpine Linux inside an Apple Containers instance.
external-sandbox-quicksand A Python web server that uses Microsoft’s Quicksand sandboxing library to bundle QEMU and Alpine Linux in a Python package.

#AIAgents #Sandboxing #PrimeRadiant #SecureCode

Source: External sandboxes for coding agents

item.title: Java4Shell: Critical Vulnerability in OpenJDK
item.description:
Java4Shell: Critical Vulnerability in OpenJDK

On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a critical memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime.

🔍 Overview

  • Java4Shell is a critical vulnerability with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 out of 10.
  • It affects Java applications and can be exploited remotely without credentials.
  • OpenJDK and Oracle released patched builds on the same day.

🧩 How it works

  • The vulnerability allows a remote attacker to send malformed Base64 data to a Java application.
  • This data overwrites memory next to the decoded output, leading to heap memory leaks and remote code execution.
  • The bug is in the handwritten assembly that handles the final characters of the input.
  • An invalid length turns into a full 64-byte write, overwriting neighboring memory.

⚙️ Key details

  • Java4Shell can be triggered by a simple input of 64 A characters followed by =.
  • The vulnerability affects various Java applications, including Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, and Jenkins.
  • Base64 is commonly used to represent binary data as text in Java applications.

🚀 Availability

  • Cloudflare has released new rules to detect malformed Base64 input patterns.
  • These rules are available on Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans and are enabled by default with the Log action.
  • Customers can review matching requests and change the rules action to Block.
  • The WAF is an additional layer of defense, not a replacement for the patch.

💡 Why it matters

  • Java4Shell can be reached through paths a WAF does not see, like outbound TLS responses.
  • The only complete fix is to update the Java runtime.
  • Cloudflare has seen no indication of Java4Shell exploitation on its infrastructure.
  • Analysts continue to monitor attack activity and will update the rules as new techniques appear.

#Java4Shell #OpenJDK #CVSS #Base64 #Security

Source: How Cloudflare WAF helps protect against Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)

item.title: Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling
item.description:
Quad9 Withdraws Public DNS Resolver from France Following Court Ruling

Last month, the Swiss non-profit foundation Quad9 announced that it will withdraw its free public DNS resolver from France. This decision followed months of litigation and a French court ruling that imposed daily financial penalties on Quad9 for failing to block domains associated with alleged copyright infringement.

🔍 Overview

The French court’s ruling forced Quad9 to choose between crippling litigation and financial penalties, or fundamentally altering its service in a way that would undermine the privacy and security of its users. Left with no good option, Quad9 is choosing to withdraw its service. This withdrawal deprives French Internet users of a trustworthy tool and creates a real risk of disruption to their daily lives.

🧩 How it works

DNS resolvers are a foundational piece of the Internet’s infrastructure.

  • Address Translation: When a user types a website name, the DNS system translates that domain name into the IP address the device needs to connect.
  • Resolution: A DNS resolver looks up that address and sends it back to the device, functioning like an operator finding a phone number in a directory.
  • Blocking Limitations: The only way a DNS resolver can block content is by declining to return the IP address for a particular website. It cannot remove the actual infringing content from the Internet, nor can it take down the servers hosting it.

⚙️ Key details

Multiple public DNS resolvers are utilized globally, but they are increasingly facing regional legal pressures:

Resolver Name Provider Details
9.9.9.9 Quad9 Withdrawing from France; used by government bodies, educational institutions, hospitals, and utilities.
1.1.1.1 Cloudflare Launched in April 2018 as a fast, reliable, privacy-first consumer DNS service that does not collect or sell user data.
8.8.8.8 Google One of the best-known public resolvers.
OpenDNS Cisco Previously withdrawn from France, Portugal, and Belgium (temporarily) under similar circumstances.

💡 Why it matters

If affected parties in France do not change their resolver before Quad9 removes its service, their Internet will fail with no explanation. Quad9 has no way to directly notify these users that their resolver will soon stop working.

This challenge is part of a broader trend. A Belgian court recently issued an order that would impose substantial penalties if Cloudflare, Google, and Cisco do not begin blocking websites through their public resolvers by early January 2027. Cloudflare, which has spent years advocating against orders of this kind, has raised concerns that unrelenting demands for blocking by public DNS resolvers will end up causing real harm to the Internet.

#DNS #InternetInfrastructure #Quad9 #Cloudflare #InternetPrivacy

Source: Quad9’s withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine

item.title: Argus AI Security Platform Launches with Self-Hosted Multi-Tenant Capabilities
item.description:
Argus AI Security Platform Launches with Self-Hosted Multi-Tenant Capabilities

A new self-hosted, multi-tenant, and MIT-licensed security platform named Argus has been released to watch cloud, identity, code, endpoints, network, and Kubernetes environments.

🔍 Overview

Argus catches attacks at machine speed, investigates them with AI agents, and contains them in seconds. The platform operates offline for air-gapped installs and ensures security data never leaves the user’s hands.

🧩 How it works

  • Nine specialist agents triage, investigate, and hunt using read-only tools.
  • Agents can propose a fix but never execute one; their one write-capable tool creates a pending request.
  • Everything agents read is treated as untrusted data so prompt injections become signals instead of hijacks.
  • Autonomous response playbooks act the moment a detection fires using a catalog of 27 typed actions.
  • Every autonomous feature ships off by default so users can enable autonomy gradually.

⚙️ Key details

  • AI Gateway: Puts OpenAI and Anthropic traffic behind org-held keys, model allowlists, data-loss prevention, prompt-injection flags, and budgets.
  • Shadow-AI Discovery: Finds services used without approval via network, cloud, and SSO telemetry.
  • Canaries: Built for agents with hidden prompt injections, agent rules files, a fake MCP server, and fake LLM API keys.
  • Attack Simulator: Replays eight AI-driven attack scenarios in an isolated sandbox tenant.
  • Pentesting: Autopilot and native autonomous pentesting plan tests and run them through a scope-checked harness.
  • Vulnerability Enrichment: CVE findings are enriched with CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list and EPSS scores, automatically raising severity.

🚀 Availability

  • Deployment options include Docker Compose for pilots, Helm for Kubernetes, and Terraform for AWS and Azure.
  • Encrypted backups run on a schedule and land on disk, S3, or Azure with single-command restore and verification checks.
  • Control mappings for SOC 2, NIST 800-171, and ISO 27001 are included.

#AISecurity #AIAgents #Cybersecurity #DevSecOps #CloudSecurity

Source: thomasunise/argus

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Following Spy Allegations and Board Investigation
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Following Spy Allegations and Board Investigation

Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following reports of a Chinese spy plot and the disclosure of multiple extramarital affairs. The resignation, announced on November 12, concludes a series of developments involving national security concerns, board investigations, and a significant decline in the company’s stock value.

🔍 Overview

According to The New York Times, Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy plot involving Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. While the CEO and company spokespeople characterized the relationship as normal, reports on November 6 indicated that China’s Ministry of State Security specifically recruited Alice Huang to spy on the executive. U.S. officials suspected she was passing information regarding Nvidia’s hardware designs or White House deliberations over trade restrictions directly to Beijing. Megaspeed had previously been investigated by the U.S. Commerce Department for allegedly smuggling advanced AI chips into China.

⚙️ Key Details

The resignation followed several internal disclosures and reports regarding the CEO’s conduct:

  • Admitted Affairs: Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised national security concerns. A second affair was subsequently reported with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care and a direct report.
  • Misleading Leadership: According to Reuters, Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.
  • Internal Reactions: Bloomberg reported that before resigning, Huang appeared “broken and shattered,” telling associates, “I’m a piece of shit.”
  • Corporate Structure: Huang managed the company with an unusual structure of approximately 60 direct reports and had no established succession plan prior to his departure.

📊 Personnel and Leadership

Name Role
Jensen Huang Resigned CEO and Co-founder
Colette Kress CFO and Interim CEO
Alice Huang Megaspeed Executive and Alleged Spy
Kimberly Powell Vice President of Health Care
Harvey Jones First Board Chair in Nvidia history
Tim Teter General Counsel
Alison Wagonfeld Chief Marketing Officer

📊 Corporate Impact

Following these developments, Nvidia’s stock price fell from an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6 to $162.85 by November 13. The company is currently facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming it deceived investors. Despite the leadership transition, Nvidia continues to manage significant capital, including $99 billion in AI lab investments and plans for $500 billion in data center infrastructure financing.

💡 Why it matters

The appointment of Harvey Jones as the company’s first board chair signals a shift in Nvidia’s corporate governance. Interim CEO Colette Kress described the transition as an “extraordinarily difficult period” for the company. The board has initiated a search for a permanent successor, evaluating both internal and external candidates to lead the company forward.

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #Cybersecurity #Semiconductors #CorporateGovernance

Source: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days

item.title: Study Finds AI Chatbots Recommending Risky and Fake Retail Websites
item.description:
Study Finds AI Chatbots Recommending Risky and Fake Retail Websites

A new study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi found that AI chatbots used by shoppers to research products or locate stores can direct users to imposter and risky websites. Across thousands of shopping-related queries, chatbots displayed risky URLs in up to 15 percent of conversations.

🔍 Overview

  • The study tested three AI engines: OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google’s Gemini, and Perplexity.
  • Podqi evaluated 6,795 answers across two testing periods in September using crafted prompts centered on 151 small and large companies.
  • Brands included in the test were Lululemon, Birkenstock, Stüssy, Madhappy, and Le Creuset.
  • Risky sites were defined as fake websites impersonating real retailers, sites selling knockoffs, reregistered former brand domains, or dead inactive sites.

📊 Engine Performance

Chatbot Risky Site Frequency Notable Behavior
Google Gemini 4% of answers Surfaced risky sites least frequently among tested models
OpenAI ChatGPT 8% of answers Warned users about surfaced risky sites 24% of the time
Perplexity 15% of answers Performed the worst, showing risky sites most frequently

⚙️ Key Details

  • Prompts asking about regional brand websites triggered risky sites more often than other prompt categories.
  • Smaller brands appear especially vulnerable, as queries regarding larger companies yielded risky sites about half as often.
  • In one conversation, Perplexity cited the wrong page as Stüssy’s official website, referring to it as “the best starting point for guaranteed authentic items.”
  • Mentions of risky sites in the study included instances where chatbots recommended the site, displayed it without comment, or warned the user about it.
  • Questions tested included: “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?”, “Where can I find [brand] online?”, and “Does [brand] ship internationally? What are their regional websites?”

💬 Stakeholder Responses

  • Podqi: CEO and cofounder Trevor West stated: “Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information.”
  • Google: Spokesperson Jessica Levis Boord said: “We take information quality seriously, and are happy to see that Gemini performed best among the products tested. We continually work to test and improve our models, and are upfront that Gemini is AI and can make mistakes, so we display links to sources alongside responses to help people verify information.”
  • OpenAI: Spokesperson Taya Christianson stated: “Our goal is for ChatGPT to connect people with reliable places to shop. We’re continuing to improve our safeguards to make potentially deceptive sites less likely to appear in shopping-related results. We appreciate researchers sharing examples that show us where we can improve the experience.”
  • Perplexity: Spokesperson Jesse Dwyer said: “Perplexity is consistently the most accurate AI on credible research benchmarks, and has been for four years. We never claim to be 100% accurate, but we do claim to be the only company relentlessly focused on it.”

#AIChatbots #Cybersecurity #ECommerce #ChatGPT #Gemini #Perplexity

Source: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds

item.title: LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling
item.description:
LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling

🔍 Overview

On 11th November 2026, a security update was released for LLM to address two vulnerabilities reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w.

⚙️ Key details

The security issues involved the accidental transmission of configured OpenAI API keys to external providers when using OpenAI-compatible API endpoints. The report identified two specific scenarios where this exposure could occur:

  • When a key named by api_key_name had not been previously stored.
  • When a ‘responses: true’ model was executed with the ‘-o chat_completions 1’ flag.

🧩 How it works

LLM utilizes a mechanism known as ’extra-openai-models.yaml’ to facilitate the use of OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. This mechanism is now managed by the new ’llm openai endpoint add’ command introduced in version 0.37.

#LLM #Security #OpenAI #API

Source: Release: llm 0.37.2

item.title: Google DeepMind Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Implementation Using AlphaProof Code AI Agents
item.description:
Google DeepMind Formally Verifies Signal Protocol Implementation Using AlphaProof Code AI Agents

Google DeepMind researchers have used AlphaProof Code, an agentic framework, to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol. This technology protects billions of private conversations in applications such as Signal and Google Messages. This work represents the first time the implementation of a widely deployed protocol has been formally verified at this depth by any method, with or without AI.

🔍 Overview

Formal verification is the process of mathematically proving that code runs correctly without flaws, offering the highest standard of security assurance. While typically labor-intensive, this process was applied to the core cryptographic code of Signal to verify its privacy guarantees against potential flaws that could expose millions of users. The agents proved that the compiled code fulfills security properties—such as maintaining message protection before and after a device is temporarily compromised—down to the exact code running on devices.

🧩 How it works

AlphaProof Code is a multi-LLM agentic framework that organizes work similarly to a research team, where human experts collaborate with AI agents to achieve formal verification.

  • Specification: Researchers worked with a mix of models to translate Signal’s security goals into formal mathematical specifications, with human experts reviewing every specification.
  • Proof Generation: AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon performed the proofs, generating over six million lines of Lean, a computer language used for the mathematical verification of code.
  • Auditing and Review: The agents audited the proofs and highlighted only one percent of the codebase for human review, allowing experts to focus their judgment where it was most needed.
  • Bug Detection: To confirm accuracy, researchers reintroduced two previously fixed bugs into an isolated version of Signal’s code. AlphaProof Code successfully produced machine-checked proofs that the buggy versions were insecure.

⚙️ Key details

Attribute Detail
Framework AlphaProof Code (multi-LLM agentic framework)
Model Engine Gemini Carbon
Language Lean (mathematical proof language)
Verification Time Four weeks (historically takes expert teams years)
Scope Production code for the Signal protocol
Lines of Lean Generated Over six million

🚀 Availability

The formal verification artifacts from this research are being open-sourced for community use. This project was developed by a team including Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli.

💡 Why it matters

Cryptographic protocols are the foundation of digital communication for banking, browsing, and messaging. While most verification stops at the design level, verifying the actual implementation helps defend against modern, agent-driven cyber threats. This achievement demonstrates how AI can bring elite security assurance to critical infrastructure, including medical device firmware and power grid software, by creating software with mathematical proof that its protections work.

#DeepMind #AlphaProof #Cybersecurity #FormalVerification #AIagents

Source: Formal Verification of Signal’s Protocol with Gemini

item.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Carbon Model with Agentic Swarm Feature
item.description:
Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Carbon Model with Agentic Swarm Feature

Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Carbon to the general public after a two‑week preview for cybersecurity defenders via its Fairwind Program. The launch adds an agentic “swarm” capability on the Antigravity platform and positions Carbon as the company’s strongest model yet.

🔍 Overview

  • Gemini 4 Carbon is described as Google’s “strongest model” and is intended to compete with top systems from Anthropic and OpenAI.
  • It “pushes the frontier even further” than the prior Argon release, which remains the preferred choice for most software‑engineering and knowledge‑work tasks.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Pricing: introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens (about one‑fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra and one‑quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2). Prices double at the end of November but remain cheaper per token than rivals.
  • Positioning: built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence—complex, multi‑step coding, debugging, and open‑ended scientific research—using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly.

🚀 Availability

  • Available today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for Business for all paying developers and enterprises.
  • Also rolled out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity.
  • No clear timeline for lower‑tier or free users.

🧩 Capabilities

  • Cybersecurity: strongest Google cybersecurity capabilities to date; leads benchmarks such as SEC‑bench Pro, ExploitGym, and CWE‑bench v1; 100 % recall on scanning and 95 % precision on triage in Project Fortify.
  • Agentic Workflows: “swarm” feature turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents that can be tracked in real time.
  • Knowledge Work: high‑precision legal, finance, and enterprise operations; generates polished spreadsheets, presentations, and reports following strict schemas.
  • Software Engineering: excels at multi‑agent collaboration for migrations, root‑cause investigations, architectural redesigns; runs build‑and‑verify loops for web apps and checks rendered UI.
  • Multimodal Reasoning: visual understanding, spatial reasoning, and 3D/ UI design; partners with Artificial Analysis for the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark.

📊 Benchmarks

  • Ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR, and Zapier’s AutomationBench with >2× lower cost per task than the next best external model.
  • In the MKA benchmark, Carbon ranks #2 while costing >6× less per task than the top model.
  • Matches best model on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation and tops 23 configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark.

🤖 Agentic “Swarm” Feature

  • Previewed on the Antigravity platform.
  • Allows a single prompt to be split among multiple agents that coordinate in real time.
  • Developers can assign Carbon to deep‑reasoning roles (architectural design, auditing) while pairing it with faster, lighter models for parallel work and adversarial verification.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Marks a decisive return for Google to the forefront of AI research after a period when frontier development was dominated by Anthropic and OpenAI.
  • Offers a competitively priced, high‑performance alternative for enterprises needing advanced reasoning, cybersecurity, and multimodal capabilities.

#GoogleAI #GeminiCarbon #AIModels

Source: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature Source: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available

item.title: AI-Powered Automation Inverts Cyber Kill Chain Leading to Large Scale Tech Breaches
item.description:
AI-Powered Automation Inverts Cyber Kill Chain Leading to Large Scale Tech Breaches

The technology industry is currently experiencing a period of continuous security breaches, characterized by the automation of the traditional cyber kill chain through AI. According to Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and lecturer at the Stanford University Cyber Policy Center, AI-enabled systems are now capable of finding vulnerabilities and writing exploits in real time, shifting these activities from a long-term research phase to immediate execution.

🧩 How it works

The traditional cyber kill chain involves upfront research, finding vulnerabilities, and writing exploits well before an attack occurs. AI has inverted this process through the following capabilities:

  • AI systems autonomously scan targets for bugs in real time.
